name: The Creative
essence: You hold real power right now, and it asks to be used steadily, at the right moment, without arrogance.
judgment: Heaven's force is at work: there is a sublime beginning, a free passage, benefit and right persistence. Whatever you start in harmony with the deep order of things can grow strong and last. Your task is to keep your energy clean and constant, like the sky that never stops turning.
image: Heaven above heaven: the sky moves on and on without tiring, and the noble person makes themselves strong and never ceases. Your strength is renewed not by bursts but by a daily, untiring rhythm.

counsel.love: Lead with warmth rather than control; your confidence is attractive when it makes room for the other person to shine as well. Keep showing up each day, as the sun does.
counsel.work: This is a time to take initiative and set the direction yourself. Act decisively, but read the stage you are at, as the dragon rises from hidden to flying only by degrees.
counsel.money: Steady effort builds lasting value now; favour sound, long-term moves over flashy ones. Overreaching at the peak is the real risk.
counsel.health: Your vitality is high, so channel it into a regular rhythm of effort and rest. Even heaven moves in cycles; do not burn through your reserves.
counsel.family: Others look to you for steadiness. Be the reliable centre without becoming the one who must decide everything.
counsel.creativity: Original ideas are flowing; begin the ambitious work. Give it daily, tireless attention rather than waiting for inspiration to strike twice.
counsel.study: Take on the difficult subject now, while your drive is strong. Practise every day, and be anxious enough at night to review what you learned.
counsel.travel: A favourable time for journeys of purpose. Go with a clear aim and keep your pace sustainable.
counsel.spirit: Feel yourself as part of a vast, ordered movement. Persistence in what is right is its own form of devotion.
counsel.conflict: You are in a strong position; use it with fairness and restraint. A dragon that climbs too high finds cause for regret.
counsel.decision: Lean yes, provided the plan is sound and you are ready to sustain it. Act, but do not force a pace beyond your stage.
counsel.timing: Soon, and with momentum, like the sun climbing toward noon on a clear summer day. Begin now and keep going.

lines: Hidden dragon. Do not act. Your strength is real but not yet recognised; gather it quietly and wait for the right hour.
Dragon appearing in the field. It furthers one to see the great person. Your abilities are starting to show; seek out a mentor or ally who can help them grow.
All day long the noble one is creatively active; at nightfall still watchful. Danger, but no blame. Rising influence brings pressure; stay diligent and alert and you will not go wrong.
Wavering flight over the depths. No blame. You stand at a threshold where you may soar or stay below; choose freely and true to yourself.
Flying dragon in the heavens. It furthers one to see the great person. You are at the height of your power; use it in partnership with others of real worth.
Arrogant dragon will have cause to repent. You have pushed past the right limit; step back before pride cuts you off from others.
scene: Six golden dragons coil and climb through towering summer clouds above a vast open plain. The lowest lies half-hidden in a misty lake, one walks the green fields, others rise higher, and the topmost soars alone near a blazing sun. Strong midday light, deep blue sky, wind streaming through the clouds.

name: The Receptive
essence: Your strength now lies in yielding, supporting and carrying, like the earth that lets everything grow.
judgment: The Receptive brings sublime success through the steadiness of a mare. If you try to lead, you will lose the way; if you follow well, you will find guidance. Friends are found in the southwest and parted from in the northeast; quiet persistence brings good fortune.
image: Earth lies upon earth, broad and deep, and the noble person with generous character carries the world. Be wide enough to hold others and the situation you are in, without needing to own it.

counsel.love: Listen more than you speak, and let the relationship unfold rather than steering it. Gentle, steady care is the deepest gift you can give now.
counsel.work: Support a capable leader or a shared project rather than pushing your own agenda. Do the work well and let credit come later, or not at all.
counsel.money: Conserve and tend what you have; this is a season for the steady accumulation that a field gives, not for bold ventures.
counsel.health: Rest, nourishment and grounding matter most. Slow down and let your body recover at its own pace.
counsel.family: Be the quiet base that others can rely on. Practical care, given without fuss, holds everyone together.
counsel.creativity: Receive before you shape: gather material, observe, take in impressions. The form will come once the ground is rich.
counsel.study: Follow a good teacher or a well-tried method rather than inventing your own. Patient absorption pays off.
counsel.travel: Go with others rather than alone, and let the route be guided by companions or circumstances. Avoid forcing an itinerary.
counsel.spirit: Practise surrender to something larger than your plans. Openness itself is a discipline.
counsel.conflict: Do not take the lead in a fight; when two dragons battle in the meadow, both bleed. Seek accommodation and let time work.
counsel.decision: Lean wait, or say yes only if you are following someone else's sound lead. Acting alone now risks losing the way.
counsel.timing: Slowly, like crops ripening in the long days of late summer. What is planted will come in its season.

lines: Hoarfrost underfoot: solid ice is not far off. Notice the small first signs of decline and act on them before they harden.
Straight, square, great. Without practice, nothing fails to further. Be simply true and upright, and things go well naturally.
Hidden lines: one can stay persevering. Keep your gifts modest and serve the work without claiming the credit; completion will come.
A tied-up sack. No blame, no praise. This is a time for strict reserve; keep your counsel and stay out of the way of danger.
A yellow lower garment brings supreme good fortune. Quiet, unshowy integrity in a central place is the highest success.
Dragons fight in the meadow; their blood is black and yellow. The yielding has tried to rule, and both sides are wounded; return to your proper place.
scene: Endless ploughed fields of golden-brown earth roll to a soft horizon under a pale sky. A dark mare walks calmly along a furrow toward the southwest. Early frost glitters on the stubble at the field's edge, and a figure in a plain yellow robe tends the soil. Low, warm afternoon light.

name: Difficulty at the Beginning
essence: Something new is pushing up through hard ground; the chaos you feel is the sign of real birth, not failure.
judgment: There is great success at the start, and persistence furthers, but do not rush to go anywhere yet. It is good to appoint helpers. Like thunder in a storm cloud, the confusion is full of life; organise it patiently rather than forcing a way through.
image: Clouds and thunder gather overhead: this is the image of the difficult start, and the noble person brings order to the tangle, like sorting threads into a weave. Your job now is to sort, structure and find your allies.

counsel.love: A new connection may be awkward or uncertain at first. Do not force a commitment; let trust form, and be clear about what you want.
counsel.work: A new venture is messy at the start. Get help, define roles and bring order to the chaos rather than charging ahead alone.
counsel.money: Early-stage finances are fragile. Keep plans modest, seek sound advice and avoid big bets until things settle.
counsel.health: Starting a new routine feels hard; take it in small steps and get support, like a sprout that needs both rain and shelter.
counsel.family: A new arrival or a new arrangement brings disorder. Share the load and accept that the early weeks are always untidy.
counsel.creativity: The first draft is a tangle; that is normal. Sort the strands, find a structure and keep going.
counsel.study: The early stages of a subject are the hardest. Find a guide, break the material into small parts and persevere.
counsel.travel: Expect delays and false starts. Go well-prepared, with a guide if you can, and do not set out in a storm without one.
counsel.spirit: The struggle of beginning is itself a teaching. Trust that order grows out of chaos when you stay with it.
counsel.conflict: The situation is too tangled for decisive action. Gather allies and clarify the facts before you press anything.
counsel.decision: Lean yes in principle, but not alone and not in haste. Start small, appoint helpers, and wait for the confusion to clear before big moves.
counsel.timing: Slowly; this is the first green shoot breaking through cold spring soil after a thunderstorm. Growth is real but will take time.

lines: Hesitation and hindrance. It furthers one to remain persevering and to appoint helpers. Do not force the obstacle; stay steady and gather support.
Difficulties pile up; horse and wagon part. Not a robber, but one who would woo. The offer of help is real but the timing is not; wait, even a long time, rather than bind yourself wrongly.
Hunting deer without a forester, one only loses the way in the forest. Without proper guidance, stop; pressing on brings humiliation.
Horse and wagon part. Strive for union; to go brings good fortune. Accept help that is offered, even if it costs your pride.
Difficulties in blessing. A little persistence brings good fortune; great persistence brings misfortune. Your good intentions are not yet understood; make small, careful moves.
Horse and wagon part; tears of blood flow. Do not stay stuck in despair; the difficulty is passing if you let go of it.
scene: A green sprout pushes up through cracked, rain-dark soil while thunderclouds churn over a misty forest. A horse stands stalled beside an overturned cart on a muddy track, and a lone hunter peers uncertainly into dense woods where a deer vanishes. Flickers of lightning, cool grey spring light, puddles everywhere.

name: Youthful Folly
essence: You do not yet know what you need to know; approach the teacher, or the lesson, with sincerity and you will be shown.
judgment: Inexperience can succeed. It is not the teacher who seeks the pupil, but the pupil who seeks the teacher. The first sincere question is answered; asking again and again out of doubt only muddies the water. Persistence in learning brings benefit.
image: A spring wells up at the foot of a mountain: the image of youth, and the noble person nourishes character by being thorough in every action. Like water that must first fill every hollow before it flows on, take your learning step by careful step.

counsel.love: There is something you do not yet understand about the other person or yourself. Ask honestly once, listen fully, and do not keep demanding reassurance.
counsel.work: Admit what you do not know and find someone who does. Being teachable now will put you far ahead later.
counsel.money: Do not act on financial matters you only half understand. Learn the basics first, or seek trustworthy advice.
counsel.health: Learn about your body's needs rather than guessing. Clear, consistent habits matter more than quick fixes.
counsel.family: If you are guiding a young person, be patient but firm; if you are the one learning, accept guidance without resentment.
counsel.creativity: Study the craft and its masters. Imitation and practice now will give you the freedom to be original later.
counsel.study: A strongly favourable sign for learning. Find a good teacher, ask sincere questions and follow through with discipline.
counsel.travel: You are in unfamiliar territory; ask locals, follow a guide and do not pretend to know the way.
counsel.spirit: Beginner's mind is a gift. Seek a tradition or teacher that has walked the path before you.
counsel.conflict: You may be missing key facts. Get informed counsel before acting; a hasty move based on ignorance will cost you.
counsel.decision: Lean wait until you understand more. Ask once, clearly, of someone who knows; then decide.
counsel.timing: Not yet: like a spring at the foot of a mountain on a misty morning, the water must find its course before it can run freely.

lines: To develop the inexperienced, it furthers to apply discipline, then to remove the fetters. Some firmness helps learning begin, but do not let it become a cage.
To bear with the inexperienced in kindness brings good fortune. Patience and generosity toward those who are learning lets you carry real responsibility.
Do not take a maiden who, seeing a man of bronze, loses herself. Do not throw yourself at what glitters; it costs you your own centre.
Entangled folly brings humiliation. Clinging to empty fantasies leaves you stuck; let reality teach you.
Childlike folly brings good fortune. Open, unpretentious readiness to learn is exactly right.
In punishing folly, it does not further to commit transgressions; it furthers only to prevent them. Correct firmly, but only to stop harm, never out of anger.
scene: A clear spring bubbles from the foot of a mist-wrapped mountain into a small pool. A young child kneels at the water's edge, gazing up at an old teacher seated on a mossy rock beneath a pine. Morning fog veils the peak, dew on ferns, soft silver light.

name: Waiting
essence: What you need is coming; wait with calm confidence and nourish yourself rather than straining toward it.
judgment: Waiting with sincerity brings light and success; persistence brings good fortune, and it furthers to cross the great water. Danger lies ahead, but strength that knows how to wait is not trapped by it. Hold steady, eat and rest well, and act when the way is clear.
image: Clouds rise up to heaven: rain is coming but has not yet fallen, and the noble person eats, drinks and is of good cheer. Do not fret over what cannot be hurried; keep yourself strong and at ease.

counsel.love: Do not press for an answer or a declaration. Enjoy the time together and let feelings ripen; what is real will come.
counsel.work: The opportunity is forming but not yet ready. Prepare thoroughly, keep your energy up and be ready to move when the moment arrives.
counsel.money: Hold steady; avoid impulsive moves while conditions are unclear. Patience is the better investment now.
counsel.health: Recovery or results need time. Eat well, rest and keep cheerful; anxious checking does not speed healing.
counsel.family: A family matter must run its course. Share meals, keep the mood warm and do not force a resolution.
counsel.creativity: The work is gestating. Feed yourself with experiences and rest; the rain of ideas will fall in its own time.
counsel.study: Results or admissions take time. Keep a steady routine and do not let waiting turn into idleness or worry.
counsel.travel: Expect delays; build in slack and enjoy the pause. A longer journey across water may be favoured once the weather clears.
counsel.spirit: Waiting is a practice of trust. Find peace in the present moment rather than leaning into the future.
counsel.conflict: Do not provoke; stay out of the mud where enemies can reach you. Time is on your side if you remain composed.
counsel.decision: Lean wait. The answer is likely yes in time, but not yet; prepare and let conditions mature.
counsel.timing: Not yet, but surely: like heavy clouds gathering on a humid summer afternoon, the rain is near but has not fallen.

lines: Waiting in the meadow. It furthers one to abide in what endures. Danger is still far off; keep your ordinary life steady and you are without blame.
Waiting on the sand. There is some small gossip; the end brings good fortune. Difficulty draws closer and people talk; stay calm and it resolves well.
Waiting in the mud brings about the arrival of the enemy. You have moved too soon into a weak position; be careful and serious.
Waiting in blood. Get out of the pit. You are in real danger; do not struggle, but hold still and let fate carry you out.
Waiting at meat and wine. Persistence brings good fortune. A pause in the midst of trouble; enjoy it and gather strength while keeping your aim.
One falls into the pit. Three uninvited guests arrive. Honour them, and in the end there is good fortune. Unexpected help may look strange; receive it with respect.
scene: A traveller sits on a riverbank meadow with bread and a jug of wine, gazing calmly across wide water toward dark billowing rainclouds over the far shore. Sand and mud stretch at the water's edge, and three strangers approach along the path. Heavy humid light, the hush before rain.

name: Conflict
essence: You may be right, but pushing the quarrel to the end will cost more than it gains; seek a fair resolution early.
judgment: You are sincere and feel blocked. Caution and stopping halfway bring good fortune; going through to the bitter end brings misfortune. It furthers to see the great person, an impartial arbiter, and it does not further to cross the great water now.
image: Heaven and water move apart, one rising and one sinking: the image of conflict, and the noble person considers the beginning carefully in all undertakings. Most disputes are avoided by clear agreements made at the start.

counsel.love: An argument is pulling you apart. Say what you need plainly, then let go of winning; the relationship matters more than the point.
counsel.work: Clarify terms, roles and expectations before going further. If a dispute has started, seek mediation rather than escalation.
counsel.money: Read contracts carefully and avoid risky ventures or lawsuits. A modest settlement now beats a costly fight later.
counsel.health: Inner tension is draining you. Release what you cannot resolve and look after your balance; stress is the real adversary.
counsel.family: Old grievances are surfacing. Step back, cool down and look for fair ground rather than proving who was wrong.
counsel.creativity: Creative disagreements need a referee or a clear brief. Agree on the vision before dividing up the work.
counsel.study: Do not let competition or an argument with a teacher derail you. Clarify the rules and focus on your own work.
counsel.travel: Not a good time for major journeys or crossings. Check bookings and terms carefully to avoid disputes.
counsel.spirit: Notice where you insist on being right. Inner peace grows from loosening that grip.
counsel.conflict: Seek an impartial judge or mediator and be ready to settle halfway. Pushing to the end brings misfortune even if you win.
counsel.decision: Lean no, especially if it means escalating or starting something risky. Resolve the disagreement before committing.
counsel.timing: Not yet: like a cold wind on a grey autumn evening, the air must clear before travel or new ventures.

lines: If one does not perpetuate the affair, there is a little gossip; in the end, good fortune. Drop the dispute early and it passes with only minor talk.

One cannot engage in conflict; one returns home and gives way. The people of the town, three hundred households, remain free of guilt. Withdrawing from a stronger opponent protects you and those around you.
To nourish oneself on ancient virtue induces persistence. Danger; in the end good fortune. Hold to what is rightfully yours and do not seek credit for service.
One cannot engage in conflict; one turns back and submits to fate, changes one's attitude and finds peace. Accepting what is right restores calm.
To contend before the great judge brings supreme good fortune. A just arbiter is available; bring your case to them.
Even if a leather belt is bestowed, by the end of a morning it will have been snatched away three times. A victory won by fighting to the end will not last.
scene: On a windswept plain, two cloaked figures argue across a deep rushing river beneath a sky split between clear high heaven and low dark clouds. A calm judge sits on a stone seat on a rise between them. A leather belt lies dropped on the bank. Grey autumn light, wind bending the reeds.

name: The Army
essence: A real challenge needs disciplined, organised effort under a trustworthy leader; gather your forces and keep them in good order.
judgment: The army needs persistence and an experienced, strong leader; then there is good fortune and no blame. Collective power must serve a just purpose and be held together by discipline and the trust of the people. Use force rarely, and only when it is right.
image: Water is hidden within the earth: the image of the army, and the noble person enlarges their following by generosity toward the people. Strength is stored in ordinary people, ready to be called on when needed.

counsel.love: A relationship needs clear commitments and shared purpose now. Work as a team, and let the steadier one take the lead in hard moments.
counsel.work: Organise people around a clear goal and a strong chain of responsibility. Choose experienced leaders, not merely eager ones.
counsel.money: Marshal your resources with discipline: a budget, a plan, a clear purpose. Scattered spending undermines the campaign.
counsel.health: Structure and routine are your allies. Treat recovery or training like a well-planned campaign with steady discipline.
counsel.family: Family members need a clear plan and fair leadership in a hard time. Be firm, just and caring with everyone's role.
counsel.creativity: A large project needs organisation: schedule, team, roles. Inspiration must be marshalled to win this.
counsel.study: Treat your study like a campaign with a clear plan. Discipline over weeks will carry you further than bursts of effort.
counsel.travel: Travel in an organised group or with a firm plan. Good logistics matter more than spontaneity now.
counsel.spirit: Spiritual practice benefits from discipline and a community. Join a sangha, a congregation, a circle.
counsel.conflict: If you must contend, do it with discipline, legitimate cause and good counsel. Do not let the inexperienced lead.
counsel.decision: Lean yes, if the cause is just and you have the right leader and organisation. Without these, wait.
counsel.timing: Soon, once ranks are in order: like a column marching out at dawn on a cold winter morning, the start must be orderly.

lines: An army must set out in proper order. If the order is not good, misfortune threatens. Begin with clear structure and a just cause.
In the midst of the army. Good fortune, no blame. The king bestows a triple decoration. The leader who shares hardship with the troops wins honour.
Perchance the army carries corpses in the wagon. Misfortune. Divided command or the wrong person in charge brings defeat.
The army retreats. No blame. Withdrawing from a fight you cannot win is wise, not shameful.
There is game in the field. It furthers to catch it. Let the eldest lead the army; the younger carries corpses. Act against a real threat, but under experienced leadership.
The great prince issues commands, founds states, vests families with fiefs. Inferior people should not be employed. After success, reward with fairness and give power only to the worthy.
scene: Orderly ranks of soldiers with banners march across a vast brown plain at dawn, a seasoned general on horseback riding among them. Beneath the earth a hidden stream glints in a cut riverbank. Breath steams in cold air; a pale sun rises over distant hills.

name: Holding Together
essence: This is a time to join with others around a true centre; ask yourself honestly whether you can be that centre, or whom you should gather around.
judgment: Holding together brings good fortune. Inquire of the oracle once more whether you have the steadiness and character for this union. Those who are uncertain gradually come; but whoever comes too late meets misfortune.
image: Water flows over the earth, filling every hollow: the image of holding together, and the ancient kings founded states and maintained friendly relations with the lords. Belonging comes naturally, as water joins water.

counsel.love: Commit, or let the other know clearly where you stand. Hesitating too long while the bond is offered can mean it slips away.
counsel.work: Join a team or alliance whose leader and values you trust. Unity of purpose is your strength now.
counsel.money: Shared resources and cooperative ventures are favoured, if your partners are sound. Do not hitch your wealth to the wrong people.
counsel.health: Community and connection support your wellbeing. Do not isolate; let others care for you and care for them.
counsel.family: Gather the family; reconnect with those you have drifted from. Be the warm centre that draws people home.
counsel.creativity: Collaborate. A shared vision with like-minded people will take you further than working alone.
counsel.study: Join a study group or find a mentor and peers. Learning together keeps you on course.
counsel.travel: Travel to meet people you care about, or go with a group. Reunions are favoured.
counsel.spirit: Find a community that shares your deepest values. Belonging is itself nourishing.
counsel.conflict: Seek allies and common ground. Unite those who can be united; do not linger outside the circle.
counsel.decision: Lean yes, but do not wait too long. Join now, with sincerity, or the chance passes.
counsel.timing: Soon: like streams joining after spring rains, the gathering happens now; late arrivals find the door closed.

lines: Hold to them in truth and loyalty; this is without blame. Truth, like a full earthen bowl, brings good fortune from unexpected quarters.
Hold to them inwardly. Persistence brings good fortune. Respond to the right call from within, without losing yourself.
You hold together with the wrong people. Be friendly, but do not give your intimacy where it does not belong.
Hold to them outwardly also. Persistence brings good fortune. Openly show your loyalty to someone worthy.
Manifestation of holding together. The king uses beaters on three sides only and forgoes game that runs off in front. Draw people freely, never by force; let those who wish to leave go.
They find no head for holding together. Misfortune. Without a true centre, or having missed the right moment, union fails.
scene: Many small streams wind across a green plain after rain, all flowing together into a shining lake at the centre. Villagers walk along the banks toward a gathering by the water, where a leader welcomes them. A royal hunt in the distance leaves an open path for deer to flee. Clear, fresh spring light.

name: The Taming Power of the Small
essence: Only small, gentle influence is possible now; refine what you can and trust that the rain will come.
judgment: The taming power of the small has success. Dense clouds roll in from the western region, yet no rain falls. Your aims are held back for a while; work by kindness and persuasion rather than force, and the time for release will arrive.
image: The wind drives across the sky: the image of small restraint, and the noble person refines the outward aspect of their nature. When you cannot do great things, polish the small ones.

counsel.love: Gentle gestures do more now than grand declarations. Small kindnesses steadily build trust.
counsel.work: Big moves are blocked; focus on details, polish, and gentle persuasion. Small wins accumulate.
counsel.money: Save in small amounts and trim small leaks. Modest steps now set up later abundance.
counsel.health: Make small, steady improvements rather than drastic changes. Gentle consistency is your best medicine.
counsel.family: Use tact and patience; a soft word goes further than insisting. Do not let small frictions turn into quarrels.
counsel.creativity: Refine and edit rather than starting anything vast. The craft is in the details right now.
counsel.study: Review, practise and polish basics. You are building quietly toward a breakthrough.
counsel.travel: Short trips are fine; major journeys may be delayed. Expect clouds but no storm.
counsel.spirit: Cultivate small daily practices. Gentleness toward yourself is a real discipline.
counsel.conflict: You cannot win by force; use courtesy and persuasion. Hold back and let small concessions open the way.
counsel.decision: Lean wait, or proceed only with something small. The larger plan is not yet ripe.
counsel.timing: Not yet: dense clouds come in from the west on a muggy summer day, but the rain holds off a little longer.

lines: Return to the way. How could there be blame in this? Good fortune. When blocked, go back to your own path; no harm in that.
Allowing oneself to be drawn back. Good fortune. Following others who return to the right course is wise.
The spokes burst out of the wagon wheels. Husband and wife roll their eyes. Forcing ahead against restraint causes breakdown and quarrels.
If you are sincere, blood vanishes and fear gives way. No blame. Honest, firm goodwill can turn aside danger even from a weaker position.
If you are sincere and loyally attached, you are rich in your neighbour. Faithfulness shared with others multiplies everyone's strength.

The rain comes, there is rest. This is due to the lasting effect of character. The moon is nearly full; if the noble person persists, misfortune. Success has arrived; stop here and do not push further.
scene: Dense dark clouds roll in from the west over a quiet farmhouse and tidy garden, while a soft wind bends the grain. A small figure gently leads a large ox on a rope. A wagon wheel with broken spokes rests by the gate. Above, a nearly full moon shows through a break in the clouds. Humid dusk light.

name: Treading
essence: You are walking close to something powerful; good manners, clarity and care let you step on the tiger's tail without being bitten.
judgment: Treading on the tail of the tiger: it does not bite the person. Success. Cheerful, courteous conduct can pass safely even through dangerous situations with those stronger than you. Know your place and keep your dignity.
image: Heaven above, the lake below: the image of treading, and the noble person distinguishes high and low and so steadies the will of the people. Clear, fair distinctions and respectful conduct give everyone solid ground.

counsel.love: Respect the other's boundaries and moods; tact and good humour carry you through a delicate time.
counsel.work: You are dealing with powerful people or a sensitive situation. Be polite, prepared and clear about roles; do not overstep.
counsel.money: Tread carefully with risky deals. Proper procedure and honest dealing keep you safe.
counsel.health: Mind your step, literally and figuratively. Careful habits and attention to warning signs keep you well.
counsel.family: Honour each person's position and feelings. Courtesy at home matters as much as in public.
counsel.creativity: Work within a form or tradition you respect; graceful mastery of the rules makes boldness possible.
counsel.study: Follow the protocol and show respect to teachers and examiners. Conduct counts alongside knowledge.
counsel.travel: Respect local customs and be alert in unfamiliar places. Careful, polite travellers come through safely.
counsel.spirit: Let your practice show in how you behave. Right conduct is the walking path of the spirit.
counsel.conflict: You face a stronger opponent. Stay courteous, calm and correct; provocation will get you bitten.
counsel.decision: Lean yes, with care. Proceed if you can do so respectfully and with full awareness of the risk.
counsel.timing: Soon, but step by step: like walking a forest path on a bright early summer morning, watch where you put your feet.

lines: Simple conduct. Progress without blame. Go your own plain way, free of ambition, and you make progress.
Treading a smooth, level course. The persistence of a quiet, solitary person brings good fortune. Keep to a modest path without entanglements.
A one-eyed person can see; a lame person can tread. Treading on the tail of the tiger, it bites the person. Misfortune. Overestimating yourself invites disaster.
Treading on the tail of the tiger. Caution and circumspection lead ultimately to good fortune. Danger is real; careful resolve carries you through.
Resolute conduct. Persistence with awareness of danger. Firmness is needed, but stay conscious of the risks.
Look to your conduct and weigh the favourable signs. When everything is fulfilled, supreme good fortune. Review the road you have walked; its fruits are the measure.
scene: A barefoot traveller in plain robes steps lightly along a sunlit forest path, carefully passing a great striped tiger lying across the way, whose tail stretches onto the trail. Ahead the path opens onto a still lake mirroring a high clear sky. Dappled early summer light through bamboo.

name: Peace
essence: Heaven and earth are in communion; this is a time of flowing harmony, to be enjoyed and wisely tended.
judgment: Peace: the small departs, the great approaches. Good fortune and success. Heaven and earth meet, high and low share one will, and good influence spreads while harm withdraws. Make the most of it, and use it to prepare for the turning that always comes.
image: Heaven and earth unite: the image of peace, and the ruler divides and completes the course of heaven and earth, furthering and regulating their gifts to help the people. Shape the abundance of the season into lasting good for everyone.

counsel.love: Love flows easily now. Enjoy the closeness and nourish it with generosity, so it remains strong when seasons change.
counsel.work: Cooperation is easy and projects move well. Build structures and partnerships that will outlast this favourable stretch.
counsel.money: Prosperity is supported; invest in what serves many, and keep some in reserve for the slope after the plain.
counsel.health: Body and mind are in good balance. Keep up the habits that got you here.
counsel.family: Harmony at home; a good time for gatherings, celebrations and mending old rifts.
counsel.creativity: Ideas and execution align. Work freely and share widely.
counsel.study: Learning comes easily. Use the flow to lay strong foundations, not just to coast.
counsel.travel: Favourable for journeys and connections. Doors open readily.
counsel.spirit: Gratitude is the right practice. Notice how heaven and earth meet in ordinary things.
counsel.conflict: A good time to make peace. Be gracious, include the distant and do not play favourites.
counsel.decision: Lean yes. Conditions favour you; act generously and with an eye to the long term.
counsel.timing: Soon, now: like the first warm days of spring when the earth wakes and everything begins to grow at once.

lines: When ribbon grass is pulled up, the sod comes with it, each according to its kind. Undertakings bring good fortune. Like-minded people rise together; move with them.

Bearing with the uncultured in gentleness, fording the river with resolution, not neglecting what is distant, not regarding one's companions. Be broad, bold and impartial, and you walk the middle way.
No plain not followed by a slope; no going not followed by a return. Remain persevering in danger; no blame. Change will come; hold to inner truth and enjoy the good while it lasts.
Fluttering down, not boasting of wealth, together with the neighbour, guileless and sincere. Those above and below meet in simple trust.
The sovereign gives his daughter in marriage. This brings blessing and supreme good fortune. Humble union between high and low brings deep blessing.
The wall falls back into the moat. Use no army now. Make your commands known within your own town. The time of peace is ending; do not resist by force, but tend what is close.
scene: A green spring valley where blue sky seems to descend to touch the blossoming earth. Farmers and nobles share a meal under flowering trees, and grass and roots are lifted together from the soil. Across a gentle river, a wedding procession crosses a bridge. Warm, clear morning light.

name: Standstill
essence: Heaven and earth are out of touch; communication is blocked, so keep your integrity, withdraw where you must, and wait for the turn.
judgment: Standstill: the wrong people hold sway, and this does not further the persistence of the noble person. The great departs, the small approaches. When channels are closed, do not compromise your values to gain advantage; quietly hold your worth.
image: Heaven and earth do not unite: the image of standstill, and the noble person falls back on inner worth to escape difficulty, not allowing themselves to be honoured with rewards. In a bad time, privacy and principle protect you.

counsel.love: Communication feels blocked. Do not force it or play games; stay true and kind, and give it time.
counsel.work: Progress is stalled and influence lies with others. Avoid compromising deals, protect your reputation and wait for a better climate.
counsel.money: A cautious season. Avoid new ventures and do not chase gains through dubious channels.
counsel.health: Energy may feel stuck. Gentle movement, rest and patience help; do not push against fatigue.
counsel.family: Distance or misunderstanding at home. Keep the door open and your words kind, without demanding closeness.
counsel.creativity: Inspiration may be dry. Keep a small practice going; avoid compromising your vision for quick approval.
counsel.study: Progress feels slow. Keep steady without expecting quick results; this is root-building time.
counsel.travel: Expect obstacles and closed doors. Postpone if you can.
counsel.spirit: Turn inward. The dark time is a test of what you truly value.
counsel.conflict: You cannot win now; do not engage on unfavourable ground. Preserve your integrity and wait.
counsel.decision: Lean no or wait. The climate is against new commitments; hold your ground.
counsel.timing: Not yet: like the closed, grey stillness of early winter when the sap has gone down and nothing grows.

lines: When ribbon grass is pulled up, the sod comes with it, each according to its kind. Persistence brings good fortune and success. Withdraw together with like-minded people, rather than serving what is wrong.
They bear and endure; this means good fortune for small people. The great person accepts the standstill and so finds success. Do not trade your principles for favour.
They bear shame. Those who rose by wrong means begin to feel it; this inner shame is the start of change.
One who acts at the command of the highest remains without blame. Those of like mind share in the blessing. When the time turns, act rightly and in concert with others.
Standstill is giving way. Good fortune for the great person. What if it should fail? Tie it to a cluster of mulberry shoots. The turn is coming; secure it with continuing care.
The standstill comes to an end. First standstill, then good fortune. Actively help the stagnation end; the blocked time does not last forever.
scene: A grey early-winter landscape where low heavy clouds hang far above frozen, barren fields that seem not to meet the sky. A lone scholar in a padded robe walks away along a bare path toward a hut in the hills. Near the hut, a cluster of mulberry shoots shows first green buds. Cold, dim light.

name: Fellowship with Others
essence: True fellowship is built in the open, around shared purpose, not in closed cliques; reach out widely.
judgment: Fellowship with others in the open: success. It furthers to cross the great water, and the persistence of the noble person furthers. Union grounded in universal concerns rather than private interests can carry people through great undertakings together.
image: Heaven together with fire: the image of fellowship, and the noble person organises the clans and makes distinctions between things. Fellowship works when each finds their place within a larger whole.

counsel.love: Be open and honest; a bond grows where there are no hidden agendas. Share friends, hopes and plans.
counsel.work: Build alliances on shared goals and transparent dealing. Look beyond your own circle for partners.
counsel.money: Cooperative or community efforts are favoured. Keep agreements open and fair to all parties.
counsel.health: Shared activity helps: group exercise, a supportive circle, honest conversation about what you need.
counsel.family: Widen the family circle; welcome newcomers and avoid favouritism. Open gatherings heal factions.
counsel.creativity: Collaborate openly. A shared mission invites contributions you could not have imagined alone.
counsel.study: Learn with others; open discussion clarifies more than solitary cramming.
counsel.travel: Travelling with companions, or to meet kindred spirits, is favoured. Crossing great waters goes well.
counsel.spirit: Seek what joins you to all people, not only your own group. Universal goodwill is the practice.
counsel.conflict: Bring hidden grievances into the open. Early tears may give way to laughter when people see their common ground.
counsel.decision: Lean yes, if done openly and together with others. Avoid acting on behalf of a narrow faction.
counsel.timing: Soon: like a bonfire on a clear summer evening that draws people out of their houses to gather.

lines: Fellowship with others at the gate. No blame. Beginnings in the open, before private ties form, are sound.
Fellowship with others in the clan. Humiliation. Favouring only your own faction leads to regret.
Weapons hidden in the thicket; climbing the high hill in front of it. For three years one does not rise up. Mistrust and hidden schemes defeat themselves.
One climbs up on the wall but cannot attack. Good fortune. Seeing the cost of conflict and stepping back is the right turn.
Fellows first weep and lament, but afterward they laugh. After great struggles they succeed in meeting. Hearts truly joined overcome separation.
Fellowship with others in the meadow. No remorse. A wider, looser fellowship, even if incomplete, leaves nothing to regret.
scene: On an open meadow at dusk, many people from different villages gather around a great bonfire whose flames rise toward a clear deep-blue sky. Two old friends embrace, laughing through tears. On a distant hill, hidden spears lie abandoned in a thicket, and a city wall stands quiet. Warm firelight against cool twilight.

name: Possession in Great Measure
essence: Great resources are within your reach; hold them with modesty and use them to bring light to others.
judgment: Great possession: supreme success. Strength combined with clarity, and a gentle position at the centre, draw great abundance. Wealth of every kind is a trust; used with clarity and generosity, it brings lasting good.
image: Fire in heaven above, shining on all things: the image of great possession, and the noble person curbs evil and furthers good, obeying the benevolent will of heaven. With much in hand, you must actively choose what to illuminate.

counsel.love: There is much to share; give it freely and without display. Abundance in love comes from generosity, not from keeping score.
counsel.work: Your efforts bear rich fruit and you have influence. Use it to support good work and good people.
counsel.money: A favourable period for resources. Stay modest, avoid showing off and share some of the harvest.
counsel.health: Energy is plentiful; stay balanced and avoid excess. Enough is a feast.
counsel.family: You can provide for others now. Do it with warmth and without making anyone feel indebted.
counsel.creativity: Your work can reach a wide audience. Let it shine for something worthwhile.
counsel.study: Knowledge is accumulating; teach and share it, and it grows further.
counsel.travel: Travels are well supported. A large vehicle for a large undertaking: plan well and go.
counsel.spirit: Recognise abundance as a gift from beyond yourself. Gratitude keeps it from turning into pride.
counsel.conflict: You hold the stronger hand; use it to promote what is right and do not humiliate others.
counsel.decision: Lean yes. You have the means; act with modesty and a sense of responsibility.
counsel.timing: Now: like the sun at midsummer noon, when everything is lit and fields stand heavy with grain.

lines: No relationship with what is harmful; there is no blame in this. If one remains conscious of difficulty, one remains without blame. Early wealth is safe if you stay aware of its dangers.
A big wagon for loading. One may undertake something. No blame. Capable helpers can carry much; take on a worthy task.
A prince offers it to the Son of Heaven. A petty person cannot do this. Place your wealth in the service of the greater good.
One makes a difference between oneself and one's neighbour. No blame. Do not compete with the powerful in display; keep your own measure.
One whose truth is accessible, yet dignified, has good fortune. Sincerity and natural dignity win hearts more than force.
Heaven itself blesses this. Good fortune. Nothing that does not further. Modesty in the midst of plenty draws blessing from above.
scene: A radiant midday sun blazes over golden fields heavy with grain. A large oxcart, piled high with sheaves, rolls toward a palace gate where a prince humbly offers baskets to a seated sovereign. Villagers share bread beneath shade trees. Brilliant midsummer light, deep blue sky.

name: Modesty
essence: Real strength that does not show off brings things to completion; let your merit speak for itself.
judgment: Modesty creates success. The noble person carries things through to the end. Heaven's way lowers the full and raises the empty; the earth's way wears down the high and fills the low. Those who stay modest are honoured and cannot be overtaken.
image: Within the earth, a mountain: the image of modesty, and the noble person reduces what is too much and increases what is too little, weighing things and making them equal. Seek a fair balance in everything you share.

counsel.love: Do not try to impress; quiet attentiveness and fairness make you deeply trustworthy. Let the other person feel valued.
counsel.work: Do excellent work without seeking credit. Your reputation will grow on its own, and you will finish what you start.
counsel.money: Moderation and fair sharing serve you well. Avoid displays of wealth; balance what is in excess with what is lacking.
counsel.health: Balance is key: trim excess, supply what is missing. Gentle, consistent care outlasts dramatic effort.
counsel.family: Level the field at home; be fair, share burdens and lift those who feel small.
counsel.creativity: Let the work, not the persona, be the point. Understatement can be powerful.
counsel.study: Stay a learner even when you know a lot. Humility keeps you teachable and steadily improving.
counsel.travel: Travel simply and respectfully. Low-key journeys bring unexpected welcomes.
counsel.spirit: Humility opens you to grace. Make room within yourself for something greater.
counsel.conflict: Seek fair balance rather than victory. If firmness is truly needed, use it without pride and only to set things right.
counsel.decision: Lean yes, if you can proceed quietly and fairly. Avoid any choice that depends on showing off.
counsel.timing: Slowly and surely: like a great mountain hidden in rolling farmland at harvest, its strength revealed over time.

lines: A modest, modest noble person may cross the great water. Good fortune. Doing a hard task simply, without fuss, carries you through.
Modesty that comes to expression. Persistence brings good fortune. Inner humility naturally shows in your bearing and is recognised.
A noble person of modesty and merit carries things to conclusion. Good fortune. Real achievements, held lightly, win lasting support.
Nothing that would not further modesty in movement. Let humility show in action, not only in words; do your share without hiding behind others.
No boasting of wealth before one's neighbour. It is favourable to attack with force. Nothing that would not further. Modesty is not weakness; firm action may be needed.
Modesty that comes to expression. It is favourable to set armies marching to chastise one's own city and one's country. Turn discipline inward; correct yourself and your own circle first.
scene: A great mountain lies low and broad beneath rolling farmland, its peak worn smooth and covered with fields. A humble farmer in plain clothes levels soil, carrying earth from a high mound to fill a hollow. Nearby a quiet river is being forded. Soft golden harvest light, wide calm sky.

name: Enthusiasm
essence: A wave of energy and joy is rising; let it move people toward a good aim, and keep your feet on the ground.
judgment: Enthusiasm: it furthers to install helpers and to set armies marching. When movement meets devotion, people follow gladly and great things can be done. Ground your excitement in preparation, so it carries others rather than sweeping you away.
image: Thunder comes resounding out of the earth: the image of enthusiasm, and the ancient kings made music to honour merit and offered it with splendour to the Supreme. Music and shared celebration unite hearts and set the rhythm for action.

counsel.love: Joy and attraction run high. Share delight freely, but notice whether shared feelings rest on something real.
counsel.work: Inspire your team and mobilise support; this is the moment to launch. Set things up so momentum does not depend on your mood alone.
counsel.money: Optimism is high; channel it into well-prepared plans. Do not let excitement cloud judgement.
counsel.health: Energy is up; enjoy movement, dance, music. Watch for overindulgence when the party feels endless.
counsel.family: Celebrate together. Festivals, music and shared rituals strengthen bonds.
counsel.creativity: Inspiration is flowing; write the song, start the work, perform. Rhythm and sound are especially favoured.
counsel.study: Learn through enjoyment and enthusiasm. Pair passion with daily structure so it lasts.
counsel.travel: A lively time for journeys, festivals and gatherings. Prepare enough that the fun does not turn into trouble.
counsel.spirit: Worship, song or dance can open the heart. Let joy become a form of devotion.
counsel.conflict: Rally allies with a hopeful vision rather than anger. Avoid boasting; it invites misfortune.
counsel.decision: Lean yes, if preparations are in place and others share your enthusiasm. Beware of acting on a passing high.
counsel.timing: Soon: like the first spring thunder that wakes the earth and sets the birds singing.

lines: Enthusiasm that expresses itself in boasting brings misfortune. Flaunting your connections or excitement isolates you.
Firm as a rock. Not a whole day. Persistence brings good fortune. Stay clear-headed amid excitement, and see the first signs quickly enough to act at once.
Enthusiasm that looks upward creates remorse. Hesitation brings remorse. Do not wait on others' favour; act from your own centre, and do not delay.
The source of enthusiasm. You achieve great things. Doubt not. You gather friends around you as a hair clasp gathers the hair. Your sincere confidence draws and holds others.
Persistently ill, and still does not die. Pressure keeps you from losing yourself in pleasure; the strain is a strange protection.
Deluded enthusiasm. But if after completion one changes, there is no blame. You have been carried away; wake up and change course.
scene: Spring thunder rumbles from dark clouds rising out of the green earth while villagers gather on a hillside, drumming, playing flutes and dancing around a bright shrine. A leader with a jade hair clasp stands at the centre as friends gather close. Birds burst from blossoming trees. Fresh, electric spring light.

name: Following
essence: You win others by first being willing to follow what is right and what the moment asks of you.
judgment: Following opens the way to great progress, provided you hold to what is right, and then no fault attaches. To be followed you must first learn to follow: bend to the time, serve a worthy aim, and do not drag others along by force. Agreement freely given lasts; agreement extracted does not.
image: Thunder has gone down into the lake, and as evening comes the wise person goes indoors to rest and recover. There are seasons for driving forward and seasons for yielding to the dark; following the rhythm of the day is itself a kind of wisdom.

counsel.love: Let the relationship move at the pace you both actually feel rather than the pace you planned. Follow your partner's lead in something small this week and notice how it softens the air between you.
counsel.work: A new direction is forming above you or around you; align with it if it is sound rather than defending the old standard out of habit. Influence comes later to those who were willing to cooperate first.
counsel.money: Go with steady, proven currents rather than the loud tip of the moment. Check whether you are following sound judgment or simply following the crowd.
counsel.health: Your body is asking you to follow its rhythms: rest when the light goes, move when energy returns. Evening wind-down matters more than any late burst of effort.
counsel.family: Someone at home needs you to go along with them for a while, not to manage them. Choosing whom you stand beside, the elder or the child, shapes what you gain and what you let go.
counsel.creativity: Follow the work where it wants to go rather than forcing your outline onto it. Thunder resting in the lake is energy held quietly; let an idea gestate overnight.
counsel.study: Find a teacher or a text worth following and commit to it for a season. Learning accelerates when you stop second-guessing every instruction.
counsel.travel: Travel with the flow of the journey: accept detours and local customs. Plan for rest in the evenings rather than packing every hour.
counsel.spirit: Devotion here means attaching yourself sincerely to what is good and letting it carry you. The deepest following is a bond held so firmly it becomes an offering.
counsel.conflict: Ask what the other side genuinely wants and whether you could support part of it. Yielding on the form while holding to principle may end the dispute faster than any victory.
counsel.decision: Lean yes, if the path you would be following is honest and well led. Lean no if you would be going along only to be liked.
counsel.timing: Not by force, and not tonight: wait for the natural turn, as the thunder sleeps in the lake through autumn and stirs again with spring.

lines: The standard changes. Old guidance shifts; staying upright brings good fortune, and stepping out past your own gate to meet others brings real achievement.
Clinging to the little boy, losing the strong man. Attaching yourself to the small and immediate costs you the larger and more mature connection.
Clinging to the strong man, letting the little boy go. You gain what you seek by choosing the worthier bond; stay steady in that choice.
Following that wins a following. Gaining adherents brings danger if it serves your own pride; sincerity and clear sight keep you free of blame.
Sincere in the excellent. Trust placed wholeheartedly in what is good brings good fortune.
Bound fast by sincere devotion. A loyalty held so firmly it becomes sacred, like the king making offerings on the western mountain.
scene: Late dusk over a broad still lake. Low thunderclouds rest on the water, faint lightning glowing within them. Along the shore a line of travelers walks behind a lantern-bearer toward a lit farmhouse, an old man leading and a small boy trailing. Reeds bend one way in the breeze. On a far western mountain a thin column of offering smoke rises.

name: Work on What Has Been Spoiled
essence: Something left to rot is now in your hands, and patient, honest repair can turn it into a fresh start.
judgment: Decay brings the possibility of great progress, and it is favorable to cross the great water. Consider carefully the three days before you begin and the three days after. What was spoiled through neglect can be mended, but only by looking squarely at how it went wrong and following through once the work is done.
image: Wind blows low beneath the mountain and stirs everything that has settled. In the same way the wise person rouses people from stagnation and nourishes their character, clearing away what has gone stale so that growth can resume.

counsel.love: An old pattern, perhaps inherited from your parents' marriage, is spoiling something good. Name it gently together and begin repairing it rather than blaming each other for it.
counsel.work: You have inherited a mess: a neglected project, a broken process, a predecessor's debt. Study how it decayed, fix the root, and plan the days after the fix as carefully as the fix itself.
counsel.money: Look for leaks you stopped noticing: subscriptions, old debts, accounts left untended. Cleaning them out now is unglamorous and exactly what the moment asks.
counsel.health: A neglected habit needs attention; tend to it with care rather than alarm. Gentle, consistent correction works better than a dramatic overhaul.
counsel.family: Family wounds passed down a generation are yours to mend now, not to punish. Be firm with your father's mistakes and gentle with your mother's, as the old lines advise.
counsel.creativity: Return to an abandoned piece and restore it. The rot is often only on the surface; underneath is a structure worth saving.
counsel.study: Go back and repair the gaps in your foundations before advancing. A few weeks of remedial work will save years of shaky building.
counsel.travel: A journey undertaken to set something right, to visit, settle, or make amends, is favored. Prepare thoroughly before leaving and allow time for follow-up after.
counsel.spirit: Spiritual life too can go stale through routine. Let a fresh wind stir what has settled, and you may rediscover why you began.
counsel.conflict: This dispute grew from a long-neglected problem. Address the original cause rather than the latest flare-up, and be prepared to own your share of the decay.
counsel.decision: Lean yes, if the decision is to fix something rather than to abandon it. Take three days to think before, and commit three days of attention after.
counsel.timing: Begin soon, but not hastily: like clearing a neglected garden in early spring, the work is ready to start, and it rewards a careful plan and steady follow-through.

lines: Setting right what the father spoiled. A child who repairs the family's errors spares the father blame; there is danger, but it ends well.
Setting right what the mother spoiled. Some damage calls for tact, not severity; do not be too unbending.
Setting right what the father spoiled, a little roughly. There may be small regrets about your manner, but no great mistake.
Tolerating what the father spoiled. Letting the decay continue out of indulgence leads to humiliation if you go on that way.
Setting right what the father spoiled, and winning praise. Repair done well earns honor and the help of others.
Not serving kings and princes. You set yourself higher aims than worldly position; withdrawing to tend your own work is right for you.
scene: Early spring in a mountain valley. A strong wind pours down the slope beneath a snow-capped peak, scattering dead leaves from an overgrown courtyard. A young man and an old woman scrub a moss-stained bronze cauldron by a cracked well. Beetles crawl from a rotted beam they have pulled away. Fresh green shoots push up among the broken flagstones.

name: Approach
essence: Good things are drawing near you now, and you meet them best with generous care rather than complacency.
judgment: Approach brings great progress and rewards steadiness on the right path. Yet a warning comes with it: by the eighth month there will be misfortune. The light is growing now, so use this season of increase well, knowing that every rising tide eventually turns.
image: The earth stands above the lake, bordering and overseeing it. So the wise person is tireless in teaching and endless in patience, sheltering and providing for others without limit.

counsel.love: Someone is drawing closer, or your bond is deepening; welcome it warmly and with attention. Do not grow lazy in affection just because things are going well.
counsel.work: Your influence is rising: you are being given more say or oversight. Lead by teaching and protecting the people under you rather than by enjoying the view from above.
counsel.money: A season of growth is here; save part of it for the leaner months that always follow. The eighth-month warning is about planning, not fear.
counsel.health: Energy and vitality are returning. Build steady habits now while it is easy, so they hold when the season turns.
counsel.family: Draw near to someone in the family who needs guidance, especially the young. Patient, repeated teaching matters more than one stern lecture.
counsel.creativity: Ideas are approaching quickly; meet them with discipline as well as delight. Finish something while momentum lasts.
counsel.study: Mentors and opportunities are close at hand. Approach them with genuine curiosity rather than flattery, and keep up the effort after the first enthusiasm.
counsel.travel: A favorable time to set out or to visit people you oversee or care for. Go in person rather than sending word.
counsel.spirit: Feel the light lengthening after a dark time. Let gratitude make you more generous, not more comfortable.
counsel.conflict: You hold the stronger position; approach the other party with fairness and some warmth. Sweet talk without substance will only make matters worse.
counsel.decision: Lean yes: the moment favors advance. Make the move while the tide is rising, and build in protection for the turn that will come.
counsel.timing: Soon: this is the lengthening light after midwinter, when each day brings a little more; act within the growing months and do not wait until late summer.

lines: Approaching together. Joining others in a shared advance; staying firm and correct brings good fortune.
Approaching together, and all goes well. Good fortune; everything furthers you.
Sweet approach. Winning people with pleasant words and ease achieves nothing; once you regret it and correct yourself, the fault fades.
Complete approach. Meeting others fully and openly, without reserve: no fault.
Wise approach. Knowing how to choose able people and let them work is the mark of a true leader; good fortune.
Greathearted approach. Coming close out of sheer generosity, returning to help others; good fortune and no blame.
scene: A low green hill descends to the edge of a wide shining lake under a pale late-winter sun. A teacher in a padded robe walks down the slope toward a cluster of children and herders waiting by the water, arms open. Willow buds show the first green. Geese return in a long line above the far shore.

name: Contemplation
essence: Step back and look clearly, at the world and at yourself, because how you see is quietly being seen by others.
judgment: The hands have been washed but the offering is not yet made: in that pause, full of sincerity, people look up with reverence. This is a moment to gaze rather than act. When you are grave and genuine, others are changed simply by watching you.
image: Wind moves across the whole earth, touching everything it passes. So the old kings traveled through the regions, observed the people, and shaped their teaching to what they saw.

counsel.love: Watch more and assume less: what does your partner actually do, day to day? Being truly seen is itself a gift you can offer.
counsel.work: Survey the whole field before you make your move. Your conduct is on display; lead by example, not by memo.
counsel.money: Review the full picture of your finances calmly before any change. Clear observation now prevents a narrow, anxious decision later.
counsel.health: Notice patterns in sleep, mood and appetite instead of reacting to single bad days. Stillness and reflection are themselves restorative.
counsel.family: Children learn from what they observe, not what they are told. Let your own steadiness be the lesson.
counsel.creativity: Spend time just looking: walk, sketch, listen. The work will come from the depth of attention you give the world.
counsel.study: Look at the subject from a height: map it before memorizing its details. Then look at yourself as a learner and adjust.
counsel.travel: A journey of observation suits this moment: go to see, not to do. A high place with a long view is ideal.
counsel.spirit: This is the hexagram of the shrine tower and the quiet moment before ritual. Practice reverent attention; contemplate your own life to know whether to advance or withdraw.
counsel.conflict: Stand back and view the dispute as an outsider would. Your calm example will influence the outcome more than another argument.
counsel.decision: Wait a little: observe until the right course becomes visible. Decide from the high tower, not from the thick of the crowd.
counsel.timing: Not yet: this is the pause of late autumn when wind sweeps the bare fields and everything can be seen; look now, act when the seeing is complete.

lines: Boyish viewing. A child's narrow view is harmless in a child but shameful in someone who should know better.
Viewing through the crack of the door. A partial, sheltered view; enough for a limited role, not for one who must lead.
Contemplating my own life. Looking honestly at your own course shows whether to advance or to retreat.
Viewing the light of the kingdom. Seeing clearly how things are governed, you are well placed to serve as a guest of the king.
Contemplating my own life. A leader who examines his own conduct is without fault.
Contemplating his life. Even from outside the fray, examining one's character keeps one free of blame.
scene: A tall wooden watchtower stands on an open plain in late autumn. Wind combs the yellowed grass flat in long waves. A robed figure stands at the top with hands folded, gazing over villages spread below. At the tower's base a child peers through a narrow door crack. A brass basin of water sits on a stone altar beside an unlit incense bowl.

name: Biting Through
essence: Something is stuck between you and union, and you must bite through it with clear, firm action.
judgment: Biting through brings success; it is favorable to let justice be administered. When an obstacle lodges between the jaws, the mouth cannot close until it is bitten through. Gentle waiting will not remove it; clear judgment and energetic action will.
image: Thunder and lightning arrive together. So the old kings made penalties clear and laws firm, showing plainly what would happen, so that order could be restored.

counsel.love: An unspoken issue, a third person, a lie, a grievance, is lodged between you. Name it honestly and deal with it; closeness returns once it is gone.
counsel.work: A blocker, a difficult person, or a broken rule is jamming everything. Address it directly through the proper channels instead of working around it forever.
counsel.money: Confront the bill, the debt or the disputed charge you have been chewing on. Clear terms and a firm stance resolve it faster than avoidance.
counsel.health: Something you keep tolerating needs firm attention, perhaps a habit, perhaps a symptom worth having checked. Act clearly, with care and without panic.
counsel.family: Rules at home need to be clear and fairly enforced. Mild, consistent consequences work better than one thunderous outburst.
counsel.creativity: There is a knot in the work you keep avoiding: the scene, the chord, the joint. Bite into that problem first; the rest will follow.
counsel.study: Stop rereading around the hard chapter. Work through it, chewing slowly until it yields.
counsel.travel: Expect bureaucratic snags: visas, inspections, fines. Have your papers in order and deal with officials patiently and plainly.
counsel.spirit: Inner clarity requires cutting through self-deception. Lightning shows things as they are; let it.
counsel.conflict: This is a hexagram of courts and fair penalties. Seek a clear ruling and firm boundaries; be just rather than vengeful.
counsel.decision: Lean yes: act decisively to remove the obstacle. Waiting will only let it harden.
counsel.timing: Soon, and quickly: like a summer storm, thunder and lightning together, strike while the matter is clear, and let the air clear after.

lines: Feet held in the stocks, toes hidden. A small first punishment stops a small wrong before it grows; no blame.
Biting through tender meat so the nose disappears. The task is easy, perhaps overdone in zeal, but no blame.
Biting old dried meat and finding poison. An old, stale matter turns unpleasant; a little humiliation, yet no blame.
Biting dried gristle and finding metal arrowheads. The obstacle is tough; recognizing the difficulty and staying firm brings good fortune.
Biting dried lean meat and finding yellow gold. Judge fairly and remain aware of danger; then there is no blame.
Neck locked in the wooden yoke, ears hidden. One who would not listen meets misfortune.
scene: A summer night in an old courtyard. Lightning splits the sky above a tiled roof while thunder rolls. Under a lantern a magistrate in dark robes sits at a low table with brush and scales. Before him a pair of carved wooden jaws clamps a bronze rod. A strip of dried meat lies on a dish beside a few scattered arrowheads and a lump of gold.

name: Grace
essence: Beauty and good form make things go more smoothly, but you should not mistake the polish for the substance.
judgment: Grace brings success, but it is favorable mainly in small matters. Adornment can lift and dignify life, giving it shape and charm. Yet it cannot decide the great questions; for those, look beneath the surface.
image: Fire burns at the foot of the mountain, lighting its slopes with color. So the wise person brings clarity to everyday affairs but does not dare to settle serious disputes by appearances alone.

counsel.love: Small gestures of care and attractiveness matter now: a well-made meal, a kind note. But let the relationship rest on who you each are, not how things look.
counsel.work: Polish the presentation, tidy the details, make it pleasant to use. Do not let a beautiful pitch substitute for a sound plan.
counsel.money: Beware spending to impress. Choose the elegant, modest option; the plain roll of silk is enough.
counsel.health: Care for your appearance is fine, but nourish what is underneath. Gentle self-care, grooming and rest support real wellbeing.
counsel.family: Rituals and small celebrations bind a family together. Keep them warm and simple, not lavish.
counsel.creativity: A wonderful time for craft, finish and ornament. Then strip back until only what is essential and lovely remains.
counsel.study: Learning to express what you know clearly and gracefully is the task now. Style serves understanding; it does not replace it.
counsel.travel: A pleasant, small journey suits: gardens, hills, a modest walk rather than a grand expedition. Leave the carriage and go on foot.
counsel.spirit: The highest grace is plain white: simplicity without decoration. Let beauty lead you toward what is real.
counsel.conflict: Courtesy and good manners will ease minor tensions. For anything serious, do not rely on charm; seek a proper judgment.
counsel.decision: Lean yes for small, pleasant things; wait for big ones. Do not let attractive packaging make the choice for you.
counsel.timing: Slowly and in small steps, like the glow of a fire at dusk lighting the hillside: lovely for an evening, not the time to remake the year.

lines: Graceful toes. Leaving the carriage and walking: choose honest effort over borrowed show.
Grooming the beard. Adornment that only follows what it is attached to; form serving the face, not leading it.
Graceful and moist. Lovely and well-favored, but steady, lasting correctness is what brings good fortune.
Grace or simplicity? A white horse comes as if on wings: not a robber, but one who comes to woo at the proper time.
Grace in the hills and gardens. The gift of silk is small and plain; there is some embarrassment, but it ends well.
Plain white grace. Unadorned simplicity carries no fault.
scene: Evening at the foot of a green mountain. A bonfire glows at its base, lighting terraced gardens and a pavilion hung with modest silk. A young man has stepped down from an ornate carriage to walk barefoot on the path. A white horse with flowing mane gallops toward the garden gate. Petals drift through warm firelight.

name: Splitting Apart
essence: Things are wearing away beneath you, and wisdom lies in holding still, protecting what is essential, and letting the rest fall.
judgment: In splitting apart it does not further you to go anywhere. The weak are pushing up and crowding out the strong; resisting directly will only speed the collapse. Stay quiet, keep your core intact, and wait, because this erosion is a phase of nature and not the end.
image: The mountain rests on the earth, worn down at its base. So those above can only keep their place by being generous to those below, strengthening the foundation on which they stand.

counsel.love: Something is eroding, perhaps trust, perhaps patience. Do not force a showdown now; protect what is still good and tend the foundation quietly.
counsel.work: Influence may be slipping away from you, or a project is losing support. Avoid bold moves; secure your base, look after your team, and wait for the turn.
counsel.money: Protect savings and avoid new ventures. Strengthen the ground floor of your finances rather than reaching for gains.
counsel.health: This is a time to conserve energy and rest rather than push. Tend gently to whatever has been worn down.
counsel.family: Household structures may be cracking. Be generous with those who depend on you; that generosity is what holds the house together.
counsel.creativity: Let the work be stripped back to its bones. What survives the paring away is the seed of the next piece.
counsel.study: Do not start an ambitious new course now. Review and consolidate what you already know.
counsel.travel: It is not a good time to set out. If you must travel, keep plans minimal and flexible.
counsel.spirit: Decay is part of the turning of the year. The large fruit left uneaten on the tree holds the seed of renewal; keep yours.
counsel.conflict: Do not escalate; the ground is not with you. Step back and let the situation exhaust itself while you protect your integrity.
counsel.decision: Lean no, or wait: this is not the moment to begin or push. Hold your position and act once the decline has run its course.
counsel.timing: Not yet: this is the bare tree in late autumn, leaves falling one by one; wait for the stillness of winter to pass and the return to come.

lines: The leg of the bed is split. Decay begins at the foundation; firmness is being undermined, and misfortune follows.
The frame of the bed is split. The erosion creeps closer; persisting stubbornly brings misfortune.
Splitting with them. Breaking away from the corrupt crowd to keep your bond with what is good: no blame.
The bed is split to the skin. The damage reaches the person itself; misfortune.
A string of fishes. Leading the weak in good order, like a queen leading her court to the king's favor; everything furthers.
A great fruit still uneaten. The wise person is given a carriage; the petty one's hut is torn apart. The seed survives the stripping.
scene: A grey late-autumn hillside. A lone stone mountain sits heavy on cracked earth, its base crumbling into scree. Nearby a wooden bed lies outdoors, its legs split and its frame splintered. Wind strips the last leaves from a gnarled tree where one large ripe fruit still hangs. A woman leads a line of maidens along the path below, like fish on a string.

name: Return
essence: After the darkest point, the light returns on its own, and you need only turn back gently toward what is good.
judgment: Return brings success. Going out and coming in meet no harm, and friends arrive without fault. The way turns back on itself, and on the seventh day comes the return; it is favorable to have somewhere to go. Renewal follows a natural cycle and should not be forced or rushed.
image: Thunder stirs deep within the earth. So at the winter solstice the old kings closed the passes; merchants and travelers stayed put, and the ruler did not tour the provinces, letting the newly returned energy rest and strengthen.

counsel.love: A relationship can return to warmth, or you can return to a healthier way of loving. Begin small and gentle; let the renewal strengthen before testing it.
counsel.work: Go back to the basics that once worked, or back to a role or project you left. Rebuild slowly; the momentum is real but still young.
counsel.money: Finances begin to recover. Return to sound habits and resist the urge to celebrate with spending before the trend is established.
counsel.health: Recovery has begun. Rest more than seems necessary; the newly returned strength needs quiet to take root.
counsel.family: Old friends and family may come back into your life. Welcome them without reopening old accounts.
counsel.creativity: Return to an early idea or your original voice. The first impulse, before you complicated it, may be the truest.
counsel.study: Go back to the beginning and review; the fundamentals will reveal something new now.
counsel.travel: A journey home, or back to a place that matters, is favored. Otherwise this is a time to stay put and rest, as at the solstice.
counsel.spirit: The return of light after the longest night: correct a small wrong turning quickly and there is no need for remorse.
counsel.conflict: Return to the original issue and to good faith. A small step back toward reconciliation now may undo a long quarrel.
counsel.decision: Lean yes, if the choice is to return to something good or correct a mistake early. Do not launch big new campaigns; protect the fresh start.
counsel.timing: Soon, in a cycle: the turning comes on the seventh day, like the winter solstice when the light begins its slow return; begin quietly now and grow.

lines: Returning from a short distance. Turning back before going far astray needs no remorse; great good fortune.
Quiet return. Returning by following a good example; good fortune.
Repeated return. Going astray and coming back again and again is dangerous, yet there is no blame in coming back.
Walking among others, returning alone. You leave the crowd to follow what is right, even if no one follows you.
Greathearted return. Returning sincerely and generously, examining yourself: no remorse.
Missing the return. Losing the way back brings calamity; armies are routed, and for ten years no recovery is possible.
scene: A snowy valley at dawn on the winter solstice. A single shaft of pale sunlight breaks over the ridge and touches a closed mountain pass where a gate stands shut. A lone traveler walks back down a winding path toward a cottage with smoke rising. Beneath the snow, a faint crack of green shows where a shoot is stirring. Distant thunder rumbles underground.

name: Innocence
essence: Act from a clean heart without calculating the reward, and you move in step with heaven.
judgment: Innocence brings supreme success and rewards steadiness on the right path. But if you are not what you ought to be, misfortune follows, and nothing is gained by setting out. Being natural and sincere aligns you with the way things truly move; scheming and hidden motives put you against it.
image: Beneath heaven, thunder rolls, and every living thing takes on its true nature. So the old kings, rich in virtue and in harmony with the seasons, nurtured all beings.

counsel.love: Love without strategy: no games, no testing. Be openly who you are and see what that draws to you.
