counsel.work: Do the work for its own sake rather than for the promotion you are counting on. Unexpected setbacks may come that are not your fault; meet them without bitterness.
counsel.money: Plow without counting on the harvest. Avoid schemes that promise easy gain; expect surprises and keep things honest.
counsel.health: An illness that comes through no fault of yours may pass without drastic remedies; seek proper care and let nature do its part. Do not invent worry where none is needed.
counsel.family: Be straightforward with family; children especially sense hidden motives. Simple honesty heals more than clever handling.
counsel.creativity: Follow the spontaneous impulse. The work flows when you stop asking whether it will sell or be praised.
counsel.study: Learn because you are curious, not to impress. The unexpected question you follow may teach you most.
counsel.travel: Expect the unexpected: plans may shift through no fault of yours. Travel light in spirit and stay honest with everyone you meet.
counsel.spirit: This is the hexagram of being without falsehood. Align your actions with your nature and with heaven's rhythm.
counsel.conflict: Make sure your own position is clean before pressing it. A stray accusation may land on you unfairly; stay calm and truthful.
counsel.decision: Lean yes, if your motives are clean and the act is natural to you. Lean no if you are scheming or forcing an outcome.
counsel.timing: Soon, when spring thunder rolls under the open sky and everything grows as it should; but if you are forcing it, not at all.

lines: Innocent action. Acting simply and from the heart brings good fortune.
Plowing without counting on the harvest. Do each task for itself, not for its reward; then going forward furthers you.
Undeserved misfortune. A tethered cow is taken by a passer-by; the traveler's gain is the villager's loss. Not your fault, yet it touches you.
Able to remain steady. Holding to what is right keeps you free of blame.
An illness not of your making. Do not reach for drastic remedies; it will pass of itself.
Innocent action that brings misfortune. When the time is wrong, even sincere action fails; nothing furthers now.
scene: Spring under a vast open sky. Thunderheads roll above a freshly plowed field where a farmer guides an ox without looking back at the furrows. At the field edge a tethered cow is being led away by a passing wanderer, while a villager stands startled. Wildflowers spring up everywhere in the rain-washed light.

name: The Taming Power of the Great
essence: Your great strength is being held and stored, and that discipline will become a power you can draw on.
judgment: Great taming rewards steady correctness. Not eating at home brings good fortune: it is right to serve in public and share what you have gathered. It is favorable to cross the great water. Hold your energy in check now and it will be ready when the moment for great undertakings arrives.
image: Heaven is contained within the mountain, an immense force held in stillness. So the wise person learns many words of the ancients and deeds of the past, and so builds up character.

counsel.love: Restraint now strengthens the bond: do not pour out everything at once. Steady care accumulates into something deep.
counsel.work: You have energy and ideas to spare; hold them until the structure is ready. When the time comes, step into public service or a larger role.
counsel.money: Build reserves. Accumulate steadily and resist spending your strength on impulse; a substantial opportunity may come.
counsel.health: Train gradually, as with a young bull fitted with a guard on its horns. Daily disciplined practice builds lasting strength.
counsel.family: Pass on the family's stories and wisdom. Gather the past into the present so it can sustain the young.
counsel.creativity: Study the masters before you break their rules. Your stored-up influences will power a major work.
counsel.study: An excellent time for deep study: read widely in history and classics. What you store now becomes character.
counsel.travel: A great journey or crossing is favored, especially for work or service. Prepare thoroughly and practice the skills you will need.
counsel.spirit: Contemplative discipline gathers spiritual force. Ultimately the path opens onto heaven itself.
counsel.conflict: Hold back an aggressive response; check the danger early. A firm, calm restraint disarms the other side.
counsel.decision: Lean wait, then yes: prepare and hold back until ready, then commit to the larger venture.
counsel.timing: Slowly at first, then decisively: like a mountain storing the winter's snow, the force is held now and released in a great spring flood.

lines: Danger ahead. It is better to stop than to press on.
The axle pins are taken out of the cart. You are held back by a stronger force; accept it and wait.
A good horse following others. Know the danger and stay steady; practice your driving and defense each day, and going forward furthers you.
A guard board on the young bull's horns. Restraining wildness before it grows: great good fortune.
The tusk of a gelded boar. Wildness is tamed at its root, not by force against its tusk; good fortune.
Reaching the highway of heaven. The restraint has ended and the way is fully open; success.
scene: A great mountain in late winter, its inner caves glowing with a golden light as if the sky were stored inside. In front, a young bull with a wooden guard on its horns stands calmly beside a cart with its axle pins removed. A scholar sits in a cave mouth surrounded by bamboo scrolls. A broad road climbs past the peak into open blue sky.

name: Nourishment
essence: Pay attention to what you feed yourself and others, in body, word and thought, because that is what you become.
judgment: Nourishment rewards steadiness and right choices. Look at whom and what someone nourishes, and at what they seek to fill their own mouth with, and you will know them. Care in providing nourishment, for yourself and for others, is the heart of a good life.
image: Thunder stirs at the foot of the mountain, like the jaw moving below the still upper face. So the wise person is careful with words and moderate in eating and drinking.

counsel.love: Notice what you feed each other: kindness or complaint. A shared meal and gentle words are the real nourishment of love now.
counsel.work: Ask whom your work really feeds. Choose projects that sustain you and others honestly, and speak with care in meetings.
counsel.money: Provide for your own needs first and do not envy others' portions. Avoid depending on others' handouts when you could stand on your own.
counsel.health: Diet, rest and the words you hear and say all shape your health. Seek moderation and balance; consult a professional for specific concerns.
counsel.family: You may be the one others rely on for sustenance. Feed them well, but teach them to feed themselves too.
counsel.creativity: Feed your imagination with good inputs: books, music, nature. What you take in becomes what you make.
counsel.study: Choose good teachers and sources carefully; avoid gorging on information. Digest slowly.
counsel.travel: Plan food and rest carefully on any journey. A trip to nourish someone else or to bring them provisions is favored.
counsel.spirit: Spiritual nourishment comes from looking to the true source rather than coveting others' meals. Be watchful and the source will bless you.
counsel.conflict: Guard your mouth: careless words feed disputes. Speak little and precisely.
counsel.decision: Lean yes if the choice nourishes you and those in your care; lean no if it merely satisfies a craving.
counsel.timing: Slowly, like the meals of the day: steady and regular, morning and evening, rather than one great feast.

lines: Letting go your magic tortoise and gaping at me. You abandon your own resources to envy another's food; misfortune.
Turning to the summit for nourishment, straying from the path. Seeking sustenance from the wrong quarter brings misfortune.
Turning away from nourishment. Pursuing what cannot feed you brings misfortune; for ten years nothing works.
Turning to the summit for nourishment. Seeking help from above for others' sake, watchful as a tiger with steady desire: good fortune, no blame.
Turning away from the path. Unsure of your own strength, stay steady and be guided; good fortune, but do not cross the great water.
The source of nourishment. Aware of the weight of this, you bring good fortune, and it is favorable to cross the great water.
scene: Early summer at the foot of a mountain. A wide mouth-shaped cave opens above a terraced field where thunderclouds gather. Inside, an old woman serves rice and soup to children seated in a ring. A large tortoise basks on a stone by the entrance. On a ledge above, a tiger watches, eyes bright and steady. Ripening grain fills the lower terraces.

name: Preponderance of the Great
essence: The load is too heavy for the beam, and you must act boldly but carefully to shift the weight before it breaks.
judgment: The ridgepole sags under too much weight. It is favorable to have somewhere to go; then there is success. An extraordinary situation calls for extraordinary measures, but carried out gently and with a clear aim, not in panic.
image: The lake rises above the trees and floods them. So the wise person, standing alone, is unafraid, and even withdrawing from the world, is untroubled.

counsel.love: Too much is resting on the relationship: expectations, stress, outside pressure. Lighten the load or bring in support before something cracks.
counsel.work: You are carrying far more than one role should. Redistribute the weight, renegotiate, or make a decisive change; do not just brace and hope.
counsel.money: Your finances may be overextended. Reduce leverage and create a cushion; act now, while it is still a matter of choice.
counsel.health: You are under strain beyond your usual limits. Seek support and rest, and handle yourself gently, like setting things down on soft white rushes.
counsel.family: An unusual arrangement may be right: an older person starting anew, an unconventional household. Judge by whether it brings life, not by custom.
counsel.creativity: A bold, outsized project fits the moment, but build the support structure underneath it before you raise the roof.
counsel.study: You may be overloaded with courses or commitments. Drop one so the rest can stand.
counsel.travel: Take great care; this is a time of high water. Go if you must, with careful preparation, and be prepared to go alone.
counsel.spirit: Standing alone without fear, at peace even if the world does not understand you, is the gift here.
counsel.conflict: The situation is at a breaking point. A bold but well-judged move can relieve the pressure; rigid stubbornness will bring the roof down.
counsel.decision: Lean yes to a decisive change, but carry it out with great care. Doing nothing while the beam sags is the worst choice.
counsel.timing: Soon, before the flood rises any higher: like spring floodwater climbing over the trees, it is the moment of crisis, so act now with caution.

lines: Spreading white rushes underneath. Taking great care with even the smallest support: no blame.
A dry willow sprouts at its root; an old man takes a young wife. Renewal from an unlikely source; everything furthers.
The ridgepole sags to breaking. Pushing ahead regardless of the strain brings misfortune.
The ridgepole is braced. Good fortune, but if you have other motives, there will be humiliation.
A dry willow puts forth flowers; an old woman takes a young husband. A last flowering that bears no fruit: no blame, no praise.
Wading into water over your head. Misfortune, but no blame: you went through it for something worth doing.
scene: A spring flood has risen over a riverbank, the water lapping at the branches of drowned willows. An old wooden hall stands half in the water, its massive ridgepole bowing in the middle, propped up by men with fresh timbers. White rushes are spread on the ground beneath an altar. A dry willow sprouts green shoots at its root while another bursts into pale flowers.

name: The Abysmal
essence: You are in deep water, and the way through is to keep your heart steady and keep moving like the river itself.
judgment: Danger repeated, pit upon pit. If you are sincere, your heart will find its way, and whatever you do will bring honor. Water does not shrink from danger; it fills every hollow and flows on, keeping its nature. So too you must stay true to yourself in the midst of difficulty.
image: Water flows on without pause and reaches its goal. So the wise person keeps steady in virtue and makes teaching a constant practice, repeating it until it becomes second nature.

counsel.love: There are real difficulties, perhaps repeated ones. Stay honest and emotionally present; grand gestures matter less than simple faithfulness.
counsel.work: You face one challenge after another. Concentrate on small, achievable gains rather than a dramatic escape, and keep practicing your craft.
counsel.money: Uncertain waters: avoid risky leaps. Secure the basics and aim only for modest progress until the current eases.
counsel.health: Treat challenges with patience and steady routines. Simple care, repeated faithfully, carries you through; seek appropriate support.
counsel.family: A family difficulty repeats itself. Approach it sincerely and plainly, offering simple help like a jug of wine and bowl of rice through the window.
counsel.creativity: The work is hard right now. Keep going daily; repetition is your teacher, and the flow will return.
counsel.study: Drill and repetition are favored. Return to the same material again and again until it becomes part of you.
counsel.travel: Be very careful near water and in uncertain places. If you can, wait out the danger rather than plunging ahead.
counsel.spirit: Faith here means trusting the inner current even when you cannot see the shore. Keep your heart open and true.
counsel.conflict: Do not climb out of one pit into another. Pause, study the terrain, and choose the plain, honest approach.
counsel.decision: Wait, unless you can act with a clear and sincere heart. In doubt, take only small, safe steps.
counsel.timing: Not yet: this is midwinter midnight, the river running dark and cold; keep flowing steadily and the way will open in time.

lines: Pit within the pit. Falling deeper into danger by getting used to it brings misfortune.
The ravine is dangerous. Aim only for small gains; do not try to climb out all at once.
Pit upon pit, forward and back. Whichever way you turn there is danger; stop and wait, and do not act.
A jug of wine, a bowl of rice, plain clay vessels passed through the window. Simple sincerity in hard times; in the end, no blame.
The pit is not overfilled; it is only filled to the brim. Do just enough and no more; no blame.
Bound with cords, shut in among thorns. For three years no way out is found; misfortune.
scene: Midnight in midwinter. A black river rushes through a deep double gorge, falling from pool to pool between wet cliffs. Moonlight glints on spray. On a narrow ledge, a figure lowers a clay jug and bowl through a small window cut into the rock. Further down, thorn bushes choke a dry ravine bound with old ropes.

name: The Clinging
essence: Like flame clinging to wood, your light depends on what you hold to, so choose it well and tend it with care.
judgment: The clinging rewards steady correctness and brings success. Caring for the cow brings good fortune. Fire has no shape of its own; it burns by holding fast to what feeds it. Clarity comes when you depend on what is right and cultivate a gentle, docile strength.
image: Brightness rises twice, the light doubled. So the great person, by keeping the light burning steadily, illuminates the four quarters of the world.

counsel.love: Love here burns bright when you both cling to something larger than yourselves. Avoid flaring passion that dies quickly; cherish steady warmth.
counsel.work: Your clarity and visibility are high. Depend on sound principles and good colleagues, and be the steady light others can see by.
counsel.money: Clear thinking about money serves you now. Rely on proven sources and avoid flashy gains that flare up and burn out.
counsel.health: Warmth, light and gentle routines are helpful. Balance intensity with rest; do not burn too hot.
counsel.family: Be the hearth: steady, warm and reliable. Patience with elders, like care of a gentle cow, brings good fortune.
counsel.creativity: Inspiration is radiant now. Give it a stable form to cling to, such as a routine or structure, so it lasts.
counsel.study: A time of insight: things become clear. Keep the lamp lit with daily study.
counsel.travel: Bright days for travel, especially toward the south or the sun. Do not rush; keep your direction clear.
counsel.spirit: Recognize your dependence on what sustains you, and be grateful. The light within needs fuel; tend it.
counsel.conflict: Bring the facts into the light. Clear, calm illumination resolves more than heat.
counsel.decision: Lean yes, if you can see clearly and the choice binds you to something good. Wait if you are only dazzled.
counsel.timing: Soon, in full light: noon in high summer, when everything is plain to see; act in clarity, but beware the sudden blaze that burns out.

lines: Footsteps crisscross at dawn. Beginning in confusion; be serious and attentive, and there is no blame.
Yellow light. Balance and moderation, like the warm noon sun; supreme good fortune.
Light of the setting sun. Some beat the pot and sing, others lament old age; both miss the moment, misfortune.
It comes suddenly, flares up, dies down, and is cast aside. A blaze without fuel burns out quickly.
Tears in floods, sighing and grieving. Sincere sorrow and humility turn things toward good fortune.
The king sends him out to set things right. Punish the ringleaders, spare the followers; no blame.
scene: High summer noon. Two great bonfires blaze one above the other on a terraced hillside, their light doubling across a valley. A pheasant with brilliant plumage perches on a burning branch. Below, a gentle cow is led by a herder to drink. Along the western ridge an old man beats a clay pot and sings toward the sun.

name: Influence
essence: A real connection forms when you make yourself open and receptive, letting influence pass freely between you and another.
judgment: Influence brings success; steadiness furthers, and taking a bride brings good fortune. Attraction between the strong and the yielding moves both. The secret is to influence without forcing, by keeping yourself still, empty and ready to receive.
image: A lake rests on top of a mountain, the mountain holding it gently. So the wise person welcomes others by being open, making room for them inside.

counsel.love: A strong mutual attraction is favored, especially courtship and marriage. Let the bond deepen gradually; true influence works through openness, not pressure.
counsel.work: Win people by listening, not by pushing. A good partnership or alliance can form now if you make space for others' ideas.
counsel.money: Partnerships and joint ventures are favored if both sides are truly aligned. Do not let impulse decide.
counsel.health: Listen to the subtle signals of your body before they become loud. Gentle responsiveness keeps you in balance.
counsel.family: Mutual respect is the key at home. Draw family members near by welcoming them, not by commanding them.
counsel.creativity: Collaborate or let yourself be moved by others' work. Inspiration is a matter of receptivity now.
counsel.study: An open, humble mind absorbs most. Study with a friend whose approach complements yours.
counsel.travel: Journeys to meet someone, or to be with a loved one, are favored. Let the people you meet change you a little.
counsel.spirit: Stillness invites grace. Empty yourself and the influence of the deeper world can enter.
counsel.conflict: Be receptive to what the other party actually feels. Talk alone, the jaws and the tongue, will not move them.
counsel.decision: Lean yes, especially to a union, partnership or courtship that is mutual and unforced. Wait if you are being swept along by restlessness.
counsel.timing: Soon, but gently: like spring, when the snowmelt fills a mountain lake and life stirs on its own; let it come to you.

lines: Influence in the big toe. Intention stirs but has not yet moved anything.
Influence in the calves. Moving before you are moved brings misfortune; staying put brings good fortune.
Influence in the thighs. Clinging to whoever leads; going on this way brings humiliation.
Steadiness brings good fortune and regret fades. If your mind darts back and forth, only those close to you follow your thoughts.
Influence in the back of the neck. Firm, deep conviction that does not waver: no regret.
Influence in the jaws, cheeks and tongue. Mere talk, without substance, influences nothing deep.
scene: Late spring on a mountaintop where a clear lake lies in a hollow of grey stone. A young man and a young woman sit on opposite rocks at the water's edge, leaning toward each other. Blossoms float on the surface. Mist rises from the lake into soft morning light, and a pair of mandarin ducks glide side by side.

name: Duration
essence: What lasts is built through steady commitment that adapts in form but never wavers in direction.
judgment: Duration brings success without fault, and steadiness furthers; it is favorable to have somewhere to go. Lasting things are not rigid; they renew themselves in each moment while holding to their course, like the seasons that change endlessly yet never fail.
image: Thunder and wind, always together, moving and changing. So the wise person stands firm and does not change direction.

counsel.love: A lasting relationship rests on small daily faithfulness, not grand passion. Recommit to the ordinary rhythms that hold you together.
counsel.work: Stick with the path you have chosen; consistency, not novelty, will compound now. Adjust methods without abandoning the goal.
counsel.money: Steady saving and long-term planning are favored. Avoid hasty schemes to get rich quickly.
counsel.health: Build habits you can keep for years rather than intense bursts. Constancy in rest, movement and diet sustains balance.
counsel.family: Honor the commitments that hold the household together. Reliability is the gift your family needs most.
counsel.creativity: Show up every day. The long, patient practice is what makes the breakthrough possible.
counsel.study: Long-term, steady study is favored over cramming. Persevere with one course before starting another.
counsel.travel: A long or recurring journey is favored, provided you keep to your plan and pace. Do not dart about.
counsel.spirit: Constancy in practice deepens the spirit. The way is found by walking it every day.
counsel.conflict: Hold to your principles calmly and consistently. Do not be pushed into changing course by every new gust.
counsel.decision: Lean yes, if it is a long commitment you can truly keep. Lean no if you want instant results.
counsel.timing: Slowly and steadily: like the turning of the seasons year after year, the result comes in its own time; keep faith with the long rhythm.

lines: Seeking permanence too hastily. Demanding lasting results at once brings persistent misfortune; nothing furthers.
Regret vanishes. Holding to the middle path dissolves what you feared.
Not giving duration to your character. Inconsistency brings disgrace and lingering humiliation.
No game in the field. Searching in the wrong place, however long, yields nothing.
Giving duration to your character through steadiness. Right for one who follows, wrong for one who must lead and decide.
Restlessness as a constant state. Perpetual agitation brings misfortune.
scene: A long-married elderly couple walk hand in hand along a path through an old orchard as autumn wind and distant thunder stir the trees. Leaves swirl but the deep-rooted trunks stand firm. Behind them a stone house with a smoking chimney sits on a hillside. A hunter in an empty field waits with bow lowered, the meadow bare.

name: Retreat
essence: The tide has turned against you for now, so step back in good order and keep your strength intact rather than wasting it on a fight you cannot win.
judgment: Retreat brings success; in small matters it pays to hold steady. This is not flight but a deliberate, dignified withdrawal while there is still room to choose it, so that what is good in you is not worn down by forces that are rising.
image: A mountain stands beneath the open sky, and heaven draws back from it as it climbs; so the wise person keeps petty people at a distance, not with anger but with quiet reserve. You protect your position by being courteous and unavailable, never hostile.

counsel.love: If a relationship has become a place of pressure, give it space instead of pushing harder; a calm step back shows what is truly there.
counsel.work: This is a season to consolidate, not to campaign. Let a losing battle in the office go and protect the projects that still matter.
counsel.money: Reduce exposure and keep reserves. Pulling back from a risky position early is wiser than defending it to the end.
counsel.health: Rest is part of strength now. Withdraw from what drains you and let your body recover in quiet.
counsel.family: When tempers rise, leave the room politely rather than escalating; you can return to the matter when the air has cleared.
counsel.creativity: Step away from the public eye and work privately for a while; what you make in retreat will be stronger for it.
counsel.study: Narrow your focus. Drop the distractions that have crept in and return to the core of what you are learning.
counsel.travel: A good time to leave a place that no longer suits you, or to postpone a trip into crowded or tense circumstances.
counsel.spirit: Solitude restores you. Retreat inward the way a mountain hermit does, not to escape the world but to stay clear within it.
counsel.conflict: Disengage. Keep courteous distance from an opponent who is gaining ground; argument now only feeds their momentum.
counsel.decision: Lean no, or not yet. Choosing to withdraw while you still can is the strong move here.
counsel.timing: Not now; the days are shortening. Wait as the year withdraws into late summer's decline, and let the next cycle bring your opening.

lines: Retreating at the tail. You are the last to leave and danger is close; do not start anything new, simply keep still and out of sight.
Bound with yellow oxhide. Your loyalty holds you firmly in place; stay steady beside what is right and no one can pull you away.
A retreat held back. Ties you cannot cut slow your withdrawal and bring strain; care for those who depend on you, but do not take on great affairs now.
A willing retreat. Leaving gracefully while you still have the choice serves a noble heart well, though a smaller spirit would be ruined by it.
A fine and timely retreat. You withdraw in the right way at the right moment, firmly and courteously, and good fortune follows.
A cheerful retreat. You leave with a light heart and no lingering ties; freedom itself becomes your reward, and everything goes well.
scene: A lone figure in a grey travelling cloak walks up a narrow mountain path at dusk, leading a small ox loaded with bundles. Below, a walled town glows with crowded torchlight. Above, the sky opens wide and pale, drawing away from the peaks. Pines lean in a cool wind, and a few late-summer leaves are already turning.
season: late summer, as the days begin to shorten

name: The Power of the Great
essence: You have real power behind you now, and the test is whether you use it with restraint and fairness rather than simply because you can.
judgment: Great strength: steadiness and right conduct bring benefit. Strength is rising like thunder, but true greatness lies in uniting force with what is just; power that forgets this turns into mere pushing.
image: Thunder rolls high in the heavens, vast and unmistakable; so the wise person does not set foot on any path that is not fitting. Your strength is greatest when it is held inside clear principles.

counsel.love: Your feelings are strong and you may want to sweep someone along; let them come toward you freely instead of pressing your case.
counsel.work: You have the influence to move things. Use it to do what is right, not just what is fast, and avoid forcing decisions through.
counsel.money: Confidence is high, which is exactly when to avoid reckless bets. Steady, principled choices will carry your momentum further.
counsel.health: Energy is plentiful; channel it into training with good form rather than straining past your limits.
counsel.family: Your word carries weight at home. Speak firmly but gently, and resist winning arguments just to prove you are strong.
counsel.creativity: A surge of power is available. Shape it with discipline so it becomes a finished work rather than a burst of noise.
counsel.study: You can learn quickly now; build on foundations rather than racing to the advanced material.
counsel.travel: You have the vigour for a demanding journey, but do not charge into places where you are not welcome.
counsel.spirit: Practice the strength of restraint: the thunder is great because it is rare and timely, not constant.
counsel.conflict: You may hold the upper hand; do not butt your head against the hedge. A fair settlement now beats a stubborn stalemate.
counsel.decision: Lean yes, but only if the action is fair and fitting. If it requires bending your principles, the answer is no.
counsel.timing: Soon, with power gathering like the first great thunderstorms of spring; still, move when the way opens, not before.

lines: Strength in the toes. Pushing forward from the lowest place leads to trouble; this is certain, so gather yourself before you move.
Steadiness brings good fortune. Your strength is held in balance; keep to the middle path and things will go well.
The ram butts the hedge and tangles its horns. A smaller person throws their weight around while a wiser one does not; forcing your way now only traps you.
The hedge opens and nothing is tangled. Steady effort clears the way, and your strength now rests on the sturdy axle of a great cart.
Losing the goat with ease. Let go of your stubbornness without a fight; when you give up the need to butt and push, there is nothing to regret.
The goat butts the hedge and can neither go back nor forward. Nothing helps while you strain; recognise the difficulty, and in that honesty lies good fortune.
scene: A great storm breaks over a high plateau in early spring: thunder cracks from towering clouds while a powerful ram stands at the edge of a thorny hedge, horns lowered but held still. Behind it, a heavy wooden cart with a stout axle waits on the road. Rain streaks the air and the first green shoots push through dark soil.
season: early spring, the month of the first great thunder

name: Progress
essence: Like the sun lifting over the land, you are rising into view, and your progress will be easiest when you let your own good qualities shine without grasping.
judgment: Progress: a capable leader is honoured with gifts of many horses and received three times in a single day. Recognition flows easily toward someone who serves well and is in harmony with those above and below.
image: The bright sun rises over the earth; so the wise person polishes and makes visible their own clear virtue. Your task is to brighten what is already good in you, and let it be seen.

counsel.love: Openness wins hearts now; let yourself be seen as you truly are, warmly and without performance.
counsel.work: Recognition is coming. Serve the larger goal well, credit others freely, and promotion tends to follow on its own.
counsel.money: Steady growth is favoured. Take gains calmly, and do not let worry about every rise and fall cloud your judgement.
counsel.health: Morning light, fresh air and a rhythm of rising early suit you; your vitality grows with the day.
counsel.family: Bring encouragement home; your good mood and clear attention lift everyone around you.
counsel.creativity: Show your work. This is a time for it to be seen and appreciated, so step into the light.
counsel.study: Progress is quick and visible. Share what you are learning, and teaching others will clarify it further.
counsel.travel: Journeys go well, especially those that bring you before people who can help or welcome you.
counsel.spirit: Cultivate inner brightness the way a sunrise does: quietly, steadily, without strain.
counsel.conflict: Clarity favours you. Present your case openly and calmly; hidden manoeuvres would only dim your standing.
counsel.decision: Lean yes. Advance openly and generously, without hoarding or scheming.
counsel.timing: Soon, like the sun climbing in the morning; things brighten through the day, so begin early.

lines: Advancing but pushed back. Stay steady; if others do not yet trust you, remain generous and calm, and there is no fault.
Advancing in sorrow. Keep to your path; in time you will receive great blessing from a kindly elder, like a grandmother's favour.
All are in accord. Others trust you and move with you, and any regrets fall away.
Advancing like a hoarding rat. Grasping for position in secret puts you in danger; progress built on greed cannot last.
Regrets vanish. Do not take gain and loss to heart; act with a clear mind and every step brings good fortune.
Advancing with the horns. Using force is acceptable only to set your own house in order; even then it carries danger, and persisting in it brings shame.
scene: Dawn breaks over wide flat farmland: a golden sun lifts above the horizon and floods the fields with light. Along a straight road a young official rides toward a distant palace, followed by a train of fine horses with bright harness. Peasants pause in the furrows to watch. Mist burns off the earth, and a small field rat scurries into the ditch.

name: Darkening of the Light
essence: The light is under the earth for now, so keep your inner brightness alive while showing little outwardly, and endure without giving yourself away.
judgment: When the light is wounded, it pays to stay steady in hardship. An unwise power holds sway, and the good person survives by hiding their brilliance while keeping their principles quietly intact.
image: The light has sunk into the earth; so the wise person, living among the many, veils their light and yet it still shines. You remain clear inside while appearing ordinary on the surface.

counsel.love: Be gentle and private with your feelings until the climate is kinder; trust is built quietly now, not declared.
counsel.work: Under difficult leadership, do your work well and keep your opinions close. Protect your integrity without making yourself a target.
counsel.money: Keep a low profile and conserve. This is not the moment for display or for trusting promises from unreliable sources.
counsel.health: Your reserves may be low; treat yourself with patience, rest in darkness and quiet, and let healing happen slowly.
counsel.family: If a household member is struggling or unreasonable, stay kind and steady without fighting every battle.
counsel.creativity: Work in private notebooks. Ideas germinate well underground before they are ready for light.
counsel.study: Learn quietly and deeply. Discretion now protects work that will matter later.
counsel.travel: Travel modestly and avoid drawing attention. A journey taken to leave a harmful situation can be right.
counsel.spirit: Keep a small lamp burning inside. Faithfulness to your values in the dark is the deepest kind of light.
counsel.conflict: Avoid open confrontation with a stronger opponent who is acting badly. Document, endure, and wait for the turn.
counsel.decision: Lean no for anything public or bold; lean yes for quiet steps that protect what is good.
counsel.timing: Not yet. This is the long night of deep winter; the light returns, but only after the darkest hours have passed.

lines: Light darkened in flight; the bird lowers its wings. You must go without food for a while and others may gossip, but leaving is right.
Wounded in the left thigh. You are hurt but not disabled; help others with the strength of a good horse, and good fortune follows.
Hunting in the south, the great leader of darkness is caught. Change is possible, but do not expect to set everything right at once.
Entering the left side of the belly. You see into the very heart of the darkness, and know it is time to leave through the gate and courtyard.
Darkening of the light, as with Prince Ji. Like the prince who feigned madness to survive a cruel ruler, hide your light and stay inwardly steady.
Not light but darkness. What first climbed up to heaven now plunges into the depths of the earth; the dark power exhausts itself and falls.
scene: A winter night over a dark plain: the last red glow of sunset sinks beneath the earth, leaving only a thin line of fire on the horizon. A pheasant with lowered wings flies low over frozen reeds. In a humble village hut, a scholar sits by a shuttered lamp whose light leaks through the cracks. Snow falls softly.

name: The Family
essence: Put your own house in order first, with clear and loving roles, and the strength you build there will carry outward into everything else.
judgment: The family: the woman's steadiness benefits all. A household thrives when each member is true to their place and the bonds of care are kept up through daily faithfulness; order at home becomes order in the world.
image: Wind rises out of fire, the warmth of the hearth sending its influence outward; so the wise person's words have substance and their conduct has constancy. Your influence comes from being reliably what you say you are.

counsel.love: Build a home together in small daily ways: shared meals, kept promises, kindness that does not depend on mood.
counsel.work: Treat your team like a household: clear roles, mutual care and words you back with action.
counsel.money: Manage the household budget carefully and together; good stewardship of the home's resources is a quiet treasure.
counsel.health: Regular routines, shared meals and the warmth of familiar people are your medicine now.
counsel.family: This is the heart of the reading. Strengthen traditions, mend small rifts early, and let respect and affection go hand in hand.
counsel.creativity: Draw on family memory, heritage and home life; your best material is close at hand.
counsel.study: A steady routine and a well-ordered study space will help you more than any burst of effort.
counsel.travel: Home calls. Visiting family or travelling together is favoured over solitary adventure.
counsel.spirit: Your spiritual practice is how you treat the people closest to you, day after day.
counsel.conflict: Settle disputes within the circle before they spread. Be fair but firm; too much leniency and too much severity both cost you.
counsel.decision: Lean yes if it strengthens your home and close bonds; lean no if it would unsettle them.
counsel.timing: Slowly and steadily, like the evening hour when lamps are lit and the household gathers.

lines: Firm boundaries within the family. Setting clear habits early prevents trouble, and regret disappears.
She does not follow her whims but tends to the meals within. Quiet, faithful care at the centre of the home brings good fortune.
When tempers flare at home, strictness may bring regret, yet it still leads to good. Where all is giggling and indulgence, shame comes in the end.
She is the wealth of the household. Careful, generous management brings great good fortune.
The king comes to his family. A leader who approaches with love rather than fear is welcomed; do not worry, good fortune.
Sincerity and dignity in your work. Truthfulness that commands respect brings good fortune at last.
scene: A warm farmhouse kitchen at evening: a fire burns in a clay hearth, its smoke drifting up and out through a window into a breezy autumn dusk. Three generations gather around a low table set with steaming bowls. A grandmother ladles soup while a father pours tea and children set out chopsticks. Lanterns glow and dried herbs hang from the beams.
season: autumn evening, when lamps are lit

name: Opposition
essence: You and those around you are pulling in different directions, so work with small agreements and let difference sharpen your understanding rather than harden into enmity.
judgment: Opposition: in small matters there is good fortune. When people are estranged, great undertakings fail, but modest cooperation is still possible, and the very differences between you can become complementary.
image: Fire flares upward while the lake sinks downward; so the wise person keeps their own character while living in fellowship with others. You can belong without dissolving into the crowd.

counsel.love: You and your partner see things differently right now. Do not demand agreement; find one small shared pleasure and build from there.
counsel.work: Collaboration is strained. Keep projects small and well-defined, and respect differing approaches instead of forcing consensus.
counsel.money: Avoid big joint ventures with people whose aims differ from yours; small, clear arrangements are safer.
counsel.health: Opposing pulls inside you, such as rest against drive, need balancing. Small adjustments help more than dramatic overhauls.
counsel.family: Misunderstandings at home may be more about perspective than malice. Listen for what the other person actually means.
counsel.creativity: Contrast is your friend: combine opposing ideas, colours or voices and let the tension make the work alive.
counsel.study: Study the opposing view seriously. Understanding why others disagree will deepen your own position.
counsel.travel: Expect some friction or plans going sideways; keep itineraries simple and flexible.
counsel.spirit: Hold your own truth with humility. Being different from others is not the same as being apart from them.
counsel.conflict: What looks like hostility may be suspicion born of distance. Lower your guard slightly; a misread rival can turn out to be an ally.
counsel.decision: Lean yes for small, low-stakes steps; lean no for anything that requires full agreement from people who are divided.
counsel.timing: Slowly. Like fire and water meeting at twilight, things need time before they can work together.

lines: Regret vanishes. If your horse runs off, do not chase it; it will return by itself. Meet even unpleasant people politely and you avoid mistakes.
Meeting your lord in a narrow lane. An informal, unexpected encounter can bridge a gap that formal channels could not.
The wagon dragged back, the oxen halted, the driver shamed. A bad beginning, but the end will be good.
Isolated by opposition, you meet a kindred spirit. Mutual trust carries you through danger without blame.
Regret vanishes; your companion bites through the wrappings. Someone breaks through the misunderstanding; go to them, it is no mistake.

Alone, you see your companion as a mud-covered pig, a cart full of demons. You draw the bow, then lay it down: this is no robber but a suitor. Going forward, the rain falls and tension breaks into good fortune.
scene: On a lakeshore at dusk, flames from a beacon fire leap upward while their reflection trembles on still dark water below. Two travellers stand on opposite banks, one raising a bow, then lowering it. A muddy cart with a halted ox waits on the road, and a stray horse wanders back toward its owner. Summer rain clouds gather overhead.

name: Obstruction
essence: The way ahead is blocked, so turn back toward yourself and your friends, gather help, and work on what you can change before you try again.
judgment: Obstruction: the southwest is favourable, the northeast is not. It helps to see a wise person, and steadiness brings good fortune; meeting a hard road, you pause, seek counsel and strengthen yourself rather than battering at the block.
image: Water lies upon the mountain, trapped in steep ravines; so the wise person turns their attention to themselves and refines their character. Difficulty outside becomes an invitation to grow inside.

counsel.love: If things feel stuck, look at your own part first. A quiet change in you can open a door that pushing never would.
counsel.work: A project has hit a wall. Pause, consult someone experienced, and rebuild support before advancing again.
counsel.money: Do not force a deal through obstacles. Wait, review your position and seek trustworthy advice.
counsel.health: Your body may be signalling a limit. Respect it, seek good guidance, and go gently around what hurts rather than through it.
counsel.family: When relatives are at an impasse, gather the steady ones first; together you can find a gentler route.
counsel.creativity: A block is a sign to step back. Revisit your foundations and skills; returning, not forcing, will free the work.
counsel.study: A difficult subject is resisting you. Go back to basics and find a teacher or study partner.
counsel.travel: Expect delays and rough roads. Choose easier routes, travel with companions, and do not press into dangerous terrain.
counsel.spirit: Obstacles are teachers. Use this halt to look honestly at yourself and to mature.
counsel.conflict: Do not escalate. Retreat to a position of strength, gather allies and seek a wise mediator.
counsel.decision: Lean no or wait. Going forward meets obstruction; turning back to regroup is favoured.
counsel.timing: Not yet. Like a snowbound mountain pass in early winter, the way opens later, after the thaw.

lines: Going on meets obstruction; coming back earns praise. Wait for the right moment rather than forcing ahead.
The king's servant meets obstacle after obstacle, but not through any fault of his own. Duty sometimes means walking straight into trouble for others.
Going on meets obstruction, so he turns back. Returning to those who need you is the wise choice now.
Going on meets obstruction; coming back brings union. Waiting allows you to gather the allies you need.
In the midst of the greatest obstruction, friends come. When you hold the centre faithfully, help arrives.
Going on meets obstruction; coming back brings great good fortune. Turn and help others through, and seek out the great person.
scene: A narrow mountain pass in early winter: a swollen stream tumbles over black rocks between steep cliffs, and the trail ahead vanishes under a rockfall. A traveller with a staff has turned back toward a sheltered hollow where friends tend a small fire. Snow dusts the pines, and pale light falls from the southwest across lower, gentler hills.

name: Deliverance
essence: The knot is loosening and the storm has broken, so let go of the tension, forgive what can be forgiven, and return quickly to an easy, ordinary rhythm.
judgment: Deliverance: the southwest is favourable. If there is nothing more to do, return to normal life; if something remains, attend to it promptly. Once trouble is released, do not linger in it, but clear up quickly and move on.
image: Thunder and rain set in, and the tight air breaks; so the wise person pardons mistakes and forgives wrongs. Release becomes complete when you let others off the hook as well.

counsel.love: Old hurts can be let go now. Forgiveness, not post-mortems, will restore warmth between you.
counsel.work: A crisis is resolving. Finish the essential clean-up quickly, then return to normal work without dwelling on blame.
counsel.money: Debts or pressures can be settled; take the opportunity to simplify your obligations.
counsel.health: Tension can release. Breathe, stretch, and let your body come out of its defensive crouch.
counsel.family: Clear the air with a gentle conversation, then let the past be past; small grudges keep the storm alive.
counsel.creativity: A block breaks open. Let ideas pour out like spring rain before you edit anything.
counsel.study: Clarity arrives after confusion. Tie up loose ends promptly while the understanding is fresh.
counsel.travel: Roads reopen and journeys are favoured, especially toward easier, open country. Go soon.
counsel.spirit: Release what you have been gripping. Freedom comes from forgiving yourself as much as others.
counsel.conflict: Seek pardon and offer it. A settlement is possible now; do not hold out for vindication.
counsel.decision: Lean yes, and act promptly. If nothing further is needed, simply return to calm.
counsel.timing: Soon, like the first spring thunderstorm that breaks winter's grip and loosens the buds.

lines: No blame. The difficulty is passing; rest quietly and recover.
Three foxes caught in the field, and a yellow arrow received. Root out sly influences with straightforward honesty, and good fortune follows.
Carrying a load on the back while riding in a carriage. Showing off what you have not earned invites thieves; humility protects you.
Free yourself from your big toe. Let go of a dependent, clinging tie, and a true companion will come whom you can trust.
Only the wise one can free themselves. When you truly let go of what binds you, even small-minded people see you mean it, and they withdraw.
The prince shoots a hawk on a high wall and strikes it. When the moment is ripe, remove the last obstacle decisively; everything then goes well.
scene: Early spring after a thunderstorm: rain sweeps across a valley as dark clouds break apart, and sunlight spills over fresh green fields. A hunter in a yellow robe holds a bow, three foxes slipping away into the grass. On a high city wall a hawk is struck from its perch. Swollen streams run freely and buds burst on wet branches.
season: early spring, just after the first storm

name: Decrease
essence: Less is enough now; simplify, give from the heart, and trust that a small sincere offering counts for more than a lavish one.
judgment: Decrease joined with sincerity brings great good fortune and no blame. Even two simple bowls are enough for an offering; what matters is that you give up the excess and keep the essential, so that what lies below can nourish what lies above.
image: At the foot of the mountain lies a lake, its waters feeding the heights; so the wise person restrains anger and curbs desire. You grow stronger by trimming what is wasteful in yourself.

counsel.love: Simple, honest gestures matter more than grand ones. Give attention, not spectacle.
counsel.work: Trim your commitments to what really matters. Cutting back now will make your effort more effective.
counsel.money: A time to spend less and save more. Reducing outgoings is wiser than chasing new income.
counsel.health: Lighten your load: simpler food, fewer stimulants, less overwork. Moderation restores balance.
counsel.family: Small sacrifices for each other build trust. Offer time and care rather than gifts.
counsel.creativity: Strip the work down. Fewer words, fewer colours, fewer notes; the essence shines through.
counsel.study: Focus on the few things that matter most and let peripheral reading go for now.
counsel.travel: Travel light and keep plans modest. A simple trip will satisfy more than an elaborate one.
counsel.spirit: Let go of anger and craving; emptying yourself makes room for what is real.
counsel.conflict: Giving a little ground freely can resolve what stubbornness would not. Choose what you can afford to concede.
counsel.decision: Lean yes if it means simplifying or letting something go; lean no if it means adding more.
counsel.timing: Slowly, as in late autumn when the trees drop their leaves and the land rests, preparing for renewal.

lines: Leave quickly when your task is done. Helping others is good, but weigh how much you can give without harm.
Steadiness serves; bold undertakings bring misfortune. You can help others without diminishing yourself.
Three travel together and one is lost; one travels alone and finds a companion. Twos make true bonds; let what is extra fall away.
Lessen your faults and others come gladly. Correct your own weakness, and help arrives.
Someone enriches him; ten pairs of tortoises cannot oppose it. Blessing comes that no oracle could prevent: supreme good fortune.
Increased without taking from others. Steadiness brings good fortune; you gain helpers and belong to a larger household than your own.
scene: A clear lake lies at the foot of a rugged mountain in late autumn, its mist rising to water the slopes above. On a stone ledge, a person in plain robes sets down two small earthen bowls of rice and water as an offering. Bare trees stand reflected in still water, a few red leaves floating. Two pilgrims walk the shore path together.

name: Increase
essence: A time of gain has opened, so act boldly, share what flows to you, and let the good you see in others become the good you do.
judgment: Increase: it pays to undertake something and to cross the great water. Those above give generously to those below, and everyone is lifted; this favourable season should be used for real work before it passes.
image: Wind and thunder strengthen each other; so the wise person, seeing good, copies it, and finding a fault, removes it. You grow by learning eagerly and correcting yourself without delay.

counsel.love: Generosity deepens love. Give freely and notice how warmth returns to you multiplied.
counsel.work: An excellent time to launch, expand or take on a significant project. Help colleagues rise as you rise.
counsel.money: Gains are possible; share some of them, invest in what benefits others too, and avoid hoarding.
counsel.health: Good habits take root easily now. Add one healthy practice and drop one harmful one.
counsel.family: Give your time and resources to help a family member grow; it strengthens the whole household.
counsel.creativity: Inspiration is abundant. Begin ambitious work and learn openly from people you admire.
counsel.study: You absorb new material quickly. Model yourself on good teachers and fix mistakes the moment you find them.
counsel.travel: Crossing the great water is favoured: long journeys, moves and new horizons go well.
counsel.spirit: Kindness that asks for no reward is its own blessing; be the wind that helps the thunder.
counsel.conflict: Seek outcomes where both sides gain. A generous offer now can turn rivals into partners.
counsel.decision: Lean yes. Act while the season of increase lasts, and let others share in the benefit.
counsel.timing: Soon. Like the spring wind and thunder that bring the growing season, the moment is ripe now.

lines: It pays to undertake great works. Support has been given to you; use it fully and there is supreme good fortune, without blame.
Someone enriches him; ten pairs of tortoises cannot oppose it. Stay constant and you receive blessing, as a king presents an offering before heaven.
Enriched through misfortune. Hard events can bring benefit if you stay sincere, walk the middle path and report honestly to those above you.
Walking the middle and advising the prince, who follows. You are trusted to help with a great change, like moving a capital.
With a truly kind heart, do not ask. Supreme good fortune: genuine kindness will be recognised as your virtue.
He increases no one, and someone strikes him. A heart that is not steady and gives nothing invites misfortune.
scene: A fertile river valley in spring: thunder rolls in the distance as a strong wind bends young wheat in silver waves. Farmers carry baskets of seed and share them across field boundaries. A wide river runs to the sea, where a sturdy boat with full sails sets out across the water. Blossoming trees line the banks under a bright, cloud-swept sky.

name: Breakthrough
essence: The moment to settle something has come, so speak the truth openly and firmly, but without force or rage, and the last obstacle will give way.
judgment: Breakthrough: the matter must be made known openly at the king's court, spoken truthfully even though there is danger. Tell your own people first; do not resort to arms; it pays to have a clear aim. Resolution succeeds through candour and steadiness, not violence.
image: The lake has risen up to heaven and must soon pour down as rain; so the wise person shares their riches with those below and does not rest on their merit. Abundance hoarded becomes a flood; given away, it becomes nourishment.

counsel.love: Name what needs naming. A calm, honest conversation will clear the air better than hints or ultimatums.
counsel.work: Address a lingering problem directly and transparently. Bring it to the right people, and keep your tone measured.
counsel.money: Resolve old financial matters decisively, and share good fortune rather than stockpiling it.
counsel.health: A clear decision about a habit you know harms you is called for. Make the change and tell someone, for support.
counsel.family: Speak openly about something long avoided, but without blame or force; truth spoken kindly breaks the deadlock.
counsel.creativity: Finish and release. Cut the last thing that weakens the work, then let it go out into the world.
counsel.study: Commit to a clear goal and remove the distraction that keeps undermining you.
counsel.travel: A decisive departure is favoured; make arrangements openly and stay alert to unexpected risks.
counsel.spirit: Clear away one persistent inner weakness with patient resolve, not self-punishment.
counsel.conflict: Be firm and truthful, but do not fight. Public honesty is stronger than weapons now.
counsel.decision: Lean yes. Decide and announce it plainly, while keeping guard against hidden setbacks.
counsel.timing: Soon, like the heavy clouds of early summer before the rains finally break.

lines: Strength in the forward toes. Rushing ahead before you are ready leads to a mistake you cannot carry.
A cry of alarm; armed at evening and at night. Stay watchful and you need fear nothing.
Strength in the cheekbones brings misfortune. The resolute person walks alone in the rain and is splashed, and others grumble, but there is no blame.
No skin on the thighs; walking is hard. If you let yourself be led like a sheep, regret would vanish, yet you may not believe this advice.
Weeds that keep returning call for firm resolve. Walk the middle way and remain free of blame.
No cry of warning. Ignoring the danger that remains brings misfortune in the end.
scene: A high marsh lake swollen by spring rains, its waters lapping almost to the sky beneath massing storm clouds. A messenger strides toward a palace gate under a single umbrella, splattered by sudden rain. In the foreground, a farmer pulls stubborn purslane from a wet field. A small sheep follows a herder along a muddy track. Lightning glimmers far off.
season: early summer, before the rains break

name: Coming to Meet
essence: Something unexpected has come to meet you, and it may be small yet powerful, so welcome what is good in it while keeping clear limits on what could take over.
judgment: Coming to meet: the maiden is strong; do not bind yourself to her. A single yielding influence slips in beneath strength and can quickly spread, so meet it with awareness rather than surrender.
image: Beneath heaven the wind blows everywhere; so the ruler issues commands and proclaims them to the four corners. Your words and example carry far now, so be careful what you set moving.

counsel.love: An intense new attraction may be exciting but not yet trustworthy. Enjoy the meeting, but do not commit before you know them.
counsel.work: A new influence, person or idea is entering. Evaluate it carefully before letting it reshape your plans.
counsel.money: Be wary of offers that look small and harmless but could grow into obligations. Set firm limits.
counsel.health: Watch for small habits that creep in quietly. Check them early, while they are still easy to brake.
counsel.family: A newcomer or new dynamic is arriving. Be hospitable, and keep household boundaries clear.
counsel.creativity: A chance encounter can spark something wonderful; follow it, but keep your own vision at the centre.
counsel.study: New sources and ideas tempt you away. Sample them, then return to your main line of study.
counsel.travel: Unexpected meetings on the road can be rich, but keep your wits about you and protect your belongings.
counsel.spirit: Notice the first stirrings of a desire or fear before it grows. Awareness at the start is easiest.
counsel.conflict: A rival may appear modest but be ambitious. Stay courteous, limit their access, and avoid alliances you cannot control.
counsel.decision: Lean no to commitments that would tie you to an unknown force; lean yes to simply meeting and observing.
counsel.timing: Slowly and carefully. This is midsummer, when the days start to wane even at their longest.

lines: Check it with a bronze brake. Steadiness brings good fortune; letting it run brings misfortune. Even a lean pig can rampage if left unchecked.
A fish in the tank. Keep the matter in your own hands and do not hand it to guests; there is no blame.
No skin on the thighs; walking is hard. You are held back from a dangerous meeting; mindful of the danger, you avoid great error.
No fish in the tank. Neglecting those below you loses their support, and misfortune follows.
A melon sheltered under willow leaves. Hidden beauty and patience; what is good in you ripens and then falls as if from heaven.
Meeting with the horns. Holding yourself aloof is lonely and slightly humbling, but not a fault.
scene: A midsummer afternoon under a vast clear sky, a warm wind sweeping across the plain and bending tall grass. At a village crossroads, a tall young woman in bright robes meets a weathered traveller. A ripe melon lies hidden beneath trailing willow branches, a fish circles in a stone tank, and a lean pig roots by a cart wheel fitted with a bronze brake.

name: Gathering Together
essence: People and resources are coming together around you, so gather them around something worthy and stay prepared for the surprises that crowds bring.
judgment: Gathering together brings success: the king approaches his temple, it helps to see a wise leader, and generous offerings bring good fortune. A gathering holds when it centres on shared purpose and genuine reverence, not mere convenience.
image: The lake rises over the earth, collecting waters from all around; so the wise person renews their tools to meet the unforeseen. Wherever many gather, be ready for the unexpected.

counsel.love: Bring your circles together: friends, family and partner. Shared celebrations strengthen your bond.
counsel.work: Assemble the team around a clear mission and a trusted leader. Prepare contingency plans as the group grows.
counsel.money: Pooling resources can work well now, provided the purpose is shared and the safeguards are sound.
counsel.health: Community supports wellbeing: join a group, a class or a gathering. Keep your basic defences up as well.
counsel.family: Host a reunion or shared ritual. Honouring elders and traditions draws the family close.
counsel.creativity: Collaborate, curate and exhibit together. The gathered whole can be more than its parts.
counsel.study: Study groups and shared learning are especially fruitful. Gather your materials before you begin.
counsel.travel: Travel to festivals, pilgrimages or gatherings is favoured; plan for crowds and contingencies.
counsel.spirit: Collective worship, meditation or ritual strengthens you now; offer something sincere.
counsel.conflict: Bring the parties to one table with a respected mediator. Keep your guard up for sudden flare-ups.
counsel.decision: Lean yes, especially for anything that unites people around a good aim; prepare well.
counsel.timing: Soon, like the late summer harvest festival when everyone gathers at the temple.

lines: Sincere, but not to the end, there is confusion, then gathering. Call out; one clasp of the hand and you can laugh again. Going on is without blame.
Drawn in by others brings good fortune. If you are sincere, even a small offering is enough.
Gathering with sighs. Nothing seems to work, yet joining is not wrong; there is only a little embarrassment.
Great good fortune, without blame. You gather people for the common good, not for yourself.
Gathering with a rightful place. Some are not yet truly committed; constant, long-lasting integrity will win them and regret will vanish.
Lament and sighs, flowing tears. Sorrow at being apart opens the way back to belonging; there is no blame.
scene: A broad lake rises over green lowlands at harvest time, and from every road people stream toward a hilltop temple with baskets of fruit, grain and flowers. A king in ceremonial robes climbs the stone steps as drums sound. Guards polish their spears in the shade. Lanterns hang from pines, and the late summer sky glows gold.

name: Pushing Upward
essence: Like a young tree rising through the soil, you can grow steadily upward now, step by step, through quiet effort and willingness to seek help.
judgment: Pushing upward brings supreme success. Seek out those in authority and do not be anxious; setting out toward the south brings good fortune. Growth here is gentle and continuous, and it is met with welcome.
image: Within the earth, wood grows; so the wise person, devoted to virtue, piles up small things until they reach something high and great. Steady, humble accumulation becomes great height.

counsel.love: Love grows by small, consistent kindnesses. Keep tending it, and it will rise naturally.
counsel.work: Advancement is favoured through patient work and willingness to approach mentors and decision-makers.
counsel.money: Build steadily: small regular savings and investments grow upward over time.
counsel.health: Gradual progress is the right path: build strength one step at a time without rushing.
counsel.family: Support each other's growth, especially that of the young; encouragement now has lasting effects.
counsel.creativity: Work a little every day; layer by layer, the piece will rise into something substantial.
counsel.study: Each lesson builds on the last. Seek out good teachers and trust the slow climb.
counsel.travel: Journeys southward or uphill are favoured; go step by step and enjoy the ascent.
counsel.spirit: Spiritual growth is quiet and constant like a root. Daily devotion lifts you higher than any sudden leap.
counsel.conflict: Approach those with authority to resolve the matter; patient, respectful steps will carry the day.
counsel.decision: Lean yes. Go ahead in steps, without anxiety, and seek the right support.
counsel.timing: Slowly but surely, like saplings rising through late spring, adding a little height each day.

lines: Rising with welcome. Others trust you and support your ascent; great good fortune.
If you are sincere, even a small offering is enough. Honest effort counts more than display; no blame.
Rising into an empty city. The way is unexpectedly open; advance without hesitation, though do not take it for granted.
The king offers him Mount Qi. You are honoured and given a place of service; good fortune, no blame.
Steadiness brings good fortune; rising step by step. Climb the stairway calmly, one step at a time.
Rising in the dark. Blind ambition must turn into constant, quiet persistence, or it loses itself.
scene: A green hillside in late spring: young trees push upward from dark soil, new leaves glowing in warm sunlight. A long stone stairway winds up the slope toward a mountain shrine, and a lone figure climbs step by step with a small offering basket. Below lies a quiet, open city with its gates wide. Birds circle in a bright southern sky.
season: late spring, the time of vigorous growth

name: Oppression
essence: You are hemmed in and drained right now, so conserve your words, hold to your purpose, and let your inner resolve carry you through what outward effort cannot.
judgment: Oppression: success through steadiness; the great person meets good fortune and is without blame. When you speak, you are not believed, so do not rely on words; adversity tests the character and, met with calm resolve, it can strengthen rather than break you.
image: The lake has no water, its depths drained away beneath it; so the wise person stakes their life on following their will. When outward resources are spent, your purpose is what remains.

counsel.love: If you feel unheard, explaining harder may not help. Stay kind, stay true, and let constancy speak.
counsel.work: You may be constrained or underappreciated. Do the work with integrity and avoid draining arguments.
counsel.money: Resources are thin. Cut back, protect essentials and do not trust quick escapes from the strain.
counsel.health: Exhaustion is real; honour it. Rest, take nourishment and accept help, and avoid pushing past your limits.
counsel.family: In a hard season at home, keep faith with one another quietly; fewer words and more steady presence.
counsel.creativity: Even when inspiration is dry, keep a thread of practice going. Constraints can become your style.
counsel.study: If progress feels stuck, endure patiently. Understanding often arrives after the driest stretch.
counsel.travel: Journeys may be difficult or blocked. Travel only if necessary, and expect delays and fatigue.
counsel.spirit: This is a test of inner freedom. Keep your will aligned with what is right, and cheerfulness can survive hardship.
counsel.conflict: Your words may not be believed now. Avoid public arguments, rely on facts and patience, and wait for the tide to turn.
counsel.decision: Lean no or wait for anything new; lean yes for keeping faith with your deeper commitments.
counsel.timing: Not yet. Like a dry riverbed in late autumn, the water returns with the coming rains, but not today.

lines: Sitting oppressed beneath a bare tree, wandering into a dark valley; three years without seeing. Do not lose yourself in gloom; it will pass.
Oppressed amid food and drink. Comfort cannot fill an inner emptiness; help in scarlet arrives. Make offerings and do not set out yet.
Pressed by stone, leaning on thorns; entering the house, not finding the wife. Clinging to what wounds you brings misfortune.
Coming slowly, held up in a golden carriage. Wealth or rank slows your help to others and brings some shame, but the end is reached.
Nose and feet cut, oppressed by the one in purple. Joy comes slowly; offerings and patience bring release.
Tangled in creeping vines, faltering and saying, 'Any move brings regret.' Feel the regret, then act anyway; that brings good fortune.
scene: A cracked, empty lakebed in late autumn, its mud split into dry plates. A weary traveller sits beneath a bare, leafless tree at the edge of a shadowed valley. Thorny bushes and a heavy boulder block the path; creeping vines curl around a stalled golden carriage. Thin clouds drift overhead, and a faint line of rain approaches from far away.

name: The Well
essence: There is a deep source available to you and to others, so clear it, maintain it, and draw from it with care, letting it nourish everyone who comes.
judgment: The Well: the town may change but the well does not; it neither empties nor overflows, and people come and go to draw from it. If the rope falls short or the jug breaks just before the water, misfortune follows; the source is always there, but reaching it requires care and good tools.
image: Water rises over wood, as sap in plants and buckets in wells; so the wise person encourages people in their work and urges them to help one another. True nourishment flows when everyone shares the labour.

counsel.love: Return to what fundamentally nourishes your relationship; deep shared values outlast changing moods.
counsel.work: Draw on core skills and the organisation's lasting purpose. Maintain your tools and processes so they keep serving.
counsel.money: Look to dependable, long-term sources of income rather than chasing novelty; keep them well maintained.
counsel.health: Basic care is your well: water, sleep, food and movement. Keep the source clean and draw from it daily.
counsel.family: Family traditions and shared roots are a well for everyone. Keep them alive and accessible to the young.
counsel.creativity: Go deep, to the wellspring of what moves you. Classic forms and practices can refresh you.
counsel.study: Go to original sources and fundamental principles; the deeper you dig, the clearer the water.
counsel.travel: A journey to your roots, or to a place of renewal, is favoured. Prepare carefully so nothing breaks on the way.
counsel.spirit: Your inner life is a well that never runs dry; clean out its silt with regular practice.
counsel.conflict: Focus on the common good everyone shares. Point the dispute back to the source of shared need, and help each other.
counsel.decision: Lean yes, if you go about it carefully and with good tools. Do not stop short just before reaching the water.
counsel.timing: Steadily, like the quiet hours of early morning when the village gathers at the well.

lines: One does not drink the mud of the well; no animals come to an old well. Neglect leaves you unfit to nourish anyone.
Shooting fish at the wellhole; the jug is broken and leaks. Small aims and poor tools waste a good source.
The well is cleaned, but no one drinks. It is a sorrow that good water goes unused; if the ruler sees clearly, all may share the blessing.
The well is being lined with stone. Working on yourself now, instead of serving others, is time well spent; no blame.
A clear, cold spring in the well. Pure and refreshing water is ready to drink; your gifts can now nourish many.
Drawing from the well, uncovered. The source is open and dependable for all; supreme good fortune.
scene: A stone well stands at the centre of an old village square in early morning. A wooden windlass creaks as a woman lowers a bucket on a long rope, and clear cold water sparkles in the dark shaft. Villagers wait with clay jugs, one of them cracked. Willows lean over the well, and soft mist hangs over tiled roofs.

name: Revolution
essence: A real change is due, and it will hold if you make it at the right moment and with the trust of those it touches.
judgment: Only when its day has come is a change believed; then there is great success, steadiness pays, and regret falls away. Change made too early looks like whim, while change made at the ripe hour feels like the season turning, so wait until the need is plain to all and then act cleanly.
image: Fire burns inside the lake: two forces that cannot rest together, each working to overcome the other, and the wise one sets the calendar in order and makes the seasons clear. When you transform something, give people a clear sense of time and sequence so that the change becomes a rhythm they can live by rather than a shock.

counsel.love: Something in the way you love each other has outgrown its old skin; name it gently and change it together rather than letting resentment do the changing for you.
counsel.work: The old process or role no longer fits; build the case patiently, gather allies, and when the need is obvious to others, make the switch decisively.
counsel.money: A financial habit is ready to be shed; plan the new arrangement in detail before you cut over, so the change sticks instead of sliding back.
counsel.health: Your body is asking for a new routine, not a tweak; change one rhythm fully, such as sleep or meals, and give it a full season to settle.
counsel.family: A family pattern that once made sense is now a cage; propose its end calmly and explain why, and let others have their say before the new way begins.
counsel.creativity: Molt: abandon the style you have been leaning on and let the work take a new form, the way a creature leaves a shell behind.
counsel.study: Overhaul your method rather than pushing harder with the old one; a new system, set up properly, will carry you further.
counsel.travel: A journey that marks a turning point in your life is favoured; choose the departure date deliberately so it feels like a clean start.
counsel.spirit: You are not the person who first took up this path; let your practice change shape to match who you have become.
counsel.conflict: Change is warranted, but win trust before you move; reform that others believe in outlasts victory that others resent.
counsel.decision: Lean yes, if the need for change is clear to more than just you; if you are still the only one convinced, prepare and wait a little.
counsel.timing: When the day is ripe, and not before; like fire coming to the boil under water, the change happens once enough heat has built.

lines: Bound in the hide of a yellow ox. It is too early to change; hold firm and keep yourself steady until the moment comes.
On the day of its completion, make the change. Preparation is done and the time is right; moving forward now brings good fortune.
When talk of change has gone round three times, commit. Rushing brings misfortune, but once the plan has been weighed and discussed enough, you may be trusted to act.
Regret vanishes; people believe; the mandate is renewed. Your change rests on sincerity, so it will be welcomed and will bring good fortune.
The great one changes like a tiger. Your transformation is so clear and bold that others trust it even before any oracle is consulted.
The noble one changes like a leopard; the small one changes face. The great change is done; refine the details and settle down, since pushing for more now would bring misfortune.
scene: A wide mountain lake at dawn in late summer, its surface steaming where a ring of bonfires burns on rafts across the water. On the shore a tiger and a leopard stand on wet rocks, their coats bright and freshly molted, old fur drifting on the shallows. A yellow ox hide lies folded on a stone. Mist, orange firelight and pale blue sky meet.

name: The Cauldron
essence: Like a bronze cauldron that cooks raw things into offerings, your task is to turn what you have been given into something that feeds others.
judgment: The cauldron: supreme good fortune and success. A sacred vessel that transforms food for the gods and the worthy, it stands for a life set on firm legs and used for something larger than appetite, so give your gifts a proper vessel and use it well.
image: Fire burns over wood, cooking what is in the vessel, and the wise one makes their position correct and so secures their destiny. Your fate is shaped by where you stand and how upright you hold yourself; set yourself rightly and the fire of your effort will do its work.

counsel.love: Love is nourishment here: cook for each other, literally and otherwise, and build the shared rituals that make a relationship feel like a hearth.
counsel.work: You are being given a vessel, a role or platform; treat it with care, keep its legs sound, and use it to serve something bigger than your ambition.
counsel.money: Steady, well-founded resources are favoured; invest in what is solid and lasting, and keep the base strong before adding ornament.
counsel.health: Attend to what you eat and how it is prepared; slow, warm, wholesome cooking is the medicine this hexagram points to.
counsel.family: Shared meals and inherited traditions bind your family now; tend them as you would a treasured pot passed down the generations.
counsel.creativity: Your raw material is ready for the fire; refine it patiently, letting heat and time turn it into something worth offering.
counsel.study: Learn from the classics and from a respected teacher; digest slowly, and your understanding will become something you can serve to others.
counsel.travel: Travel that deepens culture, such as food, ritual or heritage, is favoured; go to learn and to share a table.
counsel.spirit: Make your daily life a vessel for something sacred; the ordinary act of cooking or serving can become an offering.
counsel.conflict: Stand on a correct and dignified footing; rivals may envy what you have, but they cannot harm what is rightly held.
