counsel.decision: Lean yes, if the plan rests on firm foundations and serves others as well as you; strengthen any weak leg first.
counsel.timing: Slowly, like a long simmer over an evening fire; the result comes when the vessel has had time to work.

lines: A cauldron with its legs turned up. Tip out what is stale before you begin; an unconventional start is no fault if it clears the way.
There is food in the cauldron. You have real substance; others may envy you, but they cannot touch you, so keep to your work.
The handles of the cauldron are altered; the pheasant fat goes uneaten. You are not yet recognised and cannot be carried, but when the rain comes regret ends and good fortune follows.
The legs of the cauldron break and the prince's meal is spilled. You took on more than you or your helpers could bear; misfortune comes from overreaching with weak support.
The cauldron has yellow handles and golden rings. Be open and modest, and the right helpers will be able to lift and carry your work; steadiness furthers.
The cauldron has rings of jade. Firm yet gentle, you bring the work to completion; great good fortune and nothing that does not further.
scene: Inside a dim stone hall on a cool autumn evening, a great three-legged bronze cauldron sits over a crackling fire of split logs. Steam rises from it into slanting gold light. Its handles gleam yellow, its carrying rings are pale green jade. Beside it, a pheasant lies on a wooden board, and robed figures wait quietly with bowls.

name: The Arousing
essence: Something startling has broken in; stay composed through the jolt and it will wake you up rather than knock you down.
judgment: Thunder brings success: it comes with a cry of fear and leaves with laughter, and though it terrifies for a hundred miles, the one who keeps calm does not drop the sacred ladle and cup. The shock is real, but your composure inside it is what turns fright into renewed life.
image: Thunder rolls upon thunder, again and again, and the wise one sets their life in order and looks within in reverent awe. Let each shock prompt honest self-examination; fear used this way becomes the root of steadiness.

counsel.love: A sudden revelation or argument has shaken you both; let the first fright pass, then talk, and you may well laugh together afterward.
counsel.work: An abrupt change has rattled the workplace; keep doing your essential tasks steadily while others scatter, and you will be the one people rely on.
counsel.money: A jolt in your finances is a wake-up call; don't panic-sell or chase losses, but review your habits with sober eyes once the noise settles.
counsel.health: A scare can be a gift if it prompts good change; take sensible care, rest your nervous system, and let the adrenaline drain before deciding anything.
counsel.family: Unexpected news has hit home; be the calm voice in the room, and let the shared shock draw the family together rather than apart.
counsel.creativity: A sudden burst of energy or a startling idea has arrived; seize the charge while it lasts and get it down before it fades.
counsel.study: A surprising result or failure is jolting you awake; treat it as a lesson, re-order your method, and you will come back sharper.
counsel.travel: Expect disruption on the road; keep your essentials close, stay calm through delays, and the trip will still reach its end.
counsel.spirit: Awe and fear are close cousins; let what frightens you deepen your reverence and draw you back to what matters.
counsel.conflict: Someone has struck suddenly; do not chase after them in the heat of the moment, and what was lost will tend to come back with time.
counsel.decision: Wait until the tremor passes; decide after the shock, not inside it, when your hands are steady again.
counsel.timing: Suddenly, like a spring storm that breaks without warning; the event comes fast, but its meaning becomes clear only after the rain.

lines: Thunder comes: oh, oh! then laughter: ha, ha! You are frightened at first, but the scare leads to wisdom and good fortune.
Thunder brings danger; your treasures are lost; climb the nine hills. Do not chase what you have lost; in seven days it returns of itself.
Thunder leaves you dazed and distraught. If the shock moves you to act, you will escape harm.
Thunder is stuck in the mud. The energy bogs down in confusion; your force is checked by circumstances, so do not waste yourself thrashing.
Thunder comes and goes; danger. Nothing essential is lost if you stay centred, and there is still work to be done.
Thunder brings ruin and wild staring. Going forward now brings misfortune; stay back while the shock has struck your neighbour and not yet you, even if others gossip.
scene: A spring night over a green valley: lightning splits a purple sky and strikes a lone pine on a hill. Below, villagers in a lantern-lit courtyard flinch, but one elder stands still at an altar, holding a bronze ladle and cup without spilling. Rain begins to fall, puddles shiver, and newly sprouted rice shines in the flashes.

name: Keeping Still
essence: This is the time to stop, quiet your restlessness, and let your mind rest where you actually are.
judgment: Keeping the back still so that the body is forgotten, walking in the courtyard without seeing the people there: no blame. True rest is not dullness but a calm in which desire and agitation fall quiet, so stop when it is time to stop and move only when it is time to move.
image: Mountains stand one behind another, and the wise one does not let their thoughts stray beyond their own situation. Your peace comes from attending to the place and moment you are in, rather than scattering yourself across every possibility.

counsel.love: Do not push or chase now; be quietly present with the person you love, and let stillness show what words cannot.
counsel.work: Pause before taking on more; finish what is in front of you and refuse to let ambition pull your attention in ten directions.
counsel.money: Hold steady; this is a time for not spending, not trading and not reacting, simply keeping what you have in good order.
counsel.health: Rest is the remedy: slow your breathing, let your shoulders and back settle, and give your body unhurried stillness.
counsel.family: Hold your tongue where words would only stir the waters; a calm, steady presence helps your family more than advice.
counsel.creativity: Let the field lie fallow for a while; sitting still with the work, without forcing, will bring the next form into view.
counsel.study: Concentrate deeply on one subject; turning away from distraction is the whole method now.
counsel.travel: Better to stay put or keep the trip short and quiet; a retreat in the hills suits you more than a busy itinerary.
counsel.spirit: Meditation is the heart of this hexagram; sit like a mountain and let thoughts pass without following them.
counsel.conflict: Stop: do not escalate, do not respond in kind; silence and firm boundaries will protect you better than argument.
counsel.decision: Lean no, or not yet; stillness is the right action until your mind is clear and the restlessness has gone.
counsel.timing: Not yet; like winter mountains under snow, this is a season of waiting, and movement will come when the thaw does.

lines: Keeping the toes still. Stop before you begin; holding back at the very start brings no blame, and steady patience serves you.
Keeping the calves still. You cannot halt the one you follow and must move with them; your heart is uneasy at being carried along.
Keeping the hips still, stiffening the spine. Forced stillness becomes rigid and painful; danger, and the heart feels smothered. Calm cannot be imposed by clenching.
Keeping the trunk still. You quiet yourself, if not yet the world; no blame.
Keeping the jaws still. Your words come in good order; speak less and better, and regret vanishes.
Noble-hearted stillness. You have reached a deep and generous calm; good fortune.
scene: Two snow-dusted mountain ranges rise one behind the other in early winter, utterly still under a pale sky. On a flat rock in the foreground a lone figure sits cross-legged with a straight back, facing the peaks, a wooden gate and an empty courtyard behind them. No wind; frost on the grass, a single crow resting on a stone wall.
season: early winter, the quiet hour before dawn

name: Development
essence: Your progress will come step by step, like a tree growing on a mountain; trust the slow way and do not skip stages.
judgment: The maiden is given in marriage: good fortune, and steadiness furthers. In the old customs a marriage unfolded through a proper sequence of steps, and so does anything lasting, which means honouring each stage as it comes.
image: A tree grows on the mountain, and the wise one dwells in dignity and goodness so as to improve the customs of others. Influence that lasts grows slowly from rooted character, the way a mountain tree becomes a landmark only over many years.

counsel.love: Let this relationship unfold properly and without rushing; courtship, trust and commitment each have their season.
counsel.work: Advancement will come through steady, visible competence; take the next proper step rather than leaping for the top.
counsel.money: Slow, regular saving and patient investment are favoured; compounding is this hexagram's natural law.
counsel.health: Build fitness gradually, a little more each week; sustainable progress beats a dramatic start that burns out.
counsel.family: Family bonds are strengthened by long, quiet faithfulness; small consistent kindnesses add up across years.
counsel.creativity: Grow the project one layer at a time; a mature work will emerge from many patient sessions rather than one burst.
counsel.study: Master the fundamentals before advancing; the wild goose rests at each stage of its flight, and so should you.
counsel.travel: Take the journey in stages, with time to settle in each place; a slow route rewards you more than a rushed one.
counsel.spirit: Spiritual growth is gradual and often invisible; keep your practice steady and trust the ripening you cannot see.
counsel.conflict: Gain ground slowly and lawfully; patience and proper procedure will carry you further than a sudden move.
counsel.decision: Lean yes, but do it in steps; commit to the next stage, not the whole leap at once.
counsel.timing: Slowly, like geese moving south in stages across an autumn sky; it will come, but in its own rhythm.

lines: The wild goose gradually nears the shore. The young one is in danger and there is talk; no blame, since a cautious start is right.
The wild goose gradually nears the cliff. Eating and drinking in peace and harmony; you have found a secure footing, so share it with others.

The wild goose gradually nears the high plain. The man goes and does not return, the woman carries a child but does not bear it: misfortune. Do not push ahead recklessly; it furthers only to guard against intruders.
The wild goose gradually nears the tree. Perhaps it finds a flat branch; you are in an awkward place, but a modest, adaptable perch keeps you from harm.
The wild goose gradually nears the summit. For three years the woman has no child, but in the end nothing can stop what is right; good fortune.
The wild goose gradually nears the high clouds. Its feathers can be used in the sacred dance; your life has become an example to others, good fortune.
scene: An autumn mountainside where a single old pine grows from rocky ground above a shore. Wild geese appear in stages along the slope: one on the beach, two on a cliff ledge, others on the high plain, in the pine branches and on the summit, with a final skein flying into bright clouds. Golden afternoon light, reeds and gentle mist.

name: The Marrying Maiden
essence: You are entering a situation where you do not hold the central place; move with tact and realism, and do not let impulse decide.
judgment: The marrying maiden: undertakings bring misfortune, and nothing furthers. A young bride entering a household as a secondary wife has no power to set the terms, so pressing for more than your position allows now only causes harm.
image: Thunder rumbles over the lake, stirring its waters, and the wise one understands what is passing in the light of the eternal end. Relationships and situations driven only by attraction are transient; keep the long view in mind and you will not be swept along.

counsel.love: Be honest with yourself about where you stand; a bond built on infatuation or unequal footing needs patience and humility, not demands.
counsel.work: You are the newcomer or the junior partner here; serve well, avoid power plays, and let your reliability speak.
counsel.money: Avoid impulsive purchases or deals that look romantic but are poorly grounded; read the terms, and keep your independence.
counsel.health: Notice where impulse is steering your habits; gentle discipline and realistic expectations will serve you better than fervour.
counsel.family: You may be in a delicate role, an in-law or step-relation perhaps; quiet courtesy will slowly earn you a true place.
counsel.creativity: Work within the constraints you have been given; a modest commission done with grace can open larger doors later.
counsel.study: You are a beginner in someone else's tradition; learn its customs before trying to reform them.
counsel.travel: Travel as a respectful guest; follow local ways, keep plans flexible, and don't expect to be treated as an insider.
counsel.spirit: Hold lightly to passing desires; seeing them against the horizon of a whole life restores your balance.
counsel.conflict: Your position is weak; avoid forcing a confrontation, and seek a fair settlement rather than a win.
counsel.decision: Lean no or wait; do not rush into an arrangement driven mainly by desire, or one in which you have no voice.
counsel.timing: Not yet; like a bride who waits for the proper season, a better time will come if you do not rush.

lines: The maiden marries as a secondary wife; the lame can still walk. Even in a lesser role you can be of real use; good fortune if you go forward modestly.
The one-eyed can still see. Disappointed in your partner or situation, you stay loyal and inwardly clear; quiet steadiness furthers.
The maiden marries as a servant. You are tempted to lower yourself to get what you want; better to wait and keep your dignity.
The maiden draws out the allotted time; a late marriage comes in its season. Waiting for the right match is not failure.
The sovereign gives his daughter in marriage; her sleeves are plainer than her maid's. Noble humility outshines show; like the nearly full moon, good fortune.
The woman holds a basket with no fruit; the man stabs the sheep and no blood flows. Form without substance; nothing here furthers.
scene: Early spring on a lakeshore under a rumbling grey-violet sky, distant thunder rippling the water. A bridal procession of lanterns and red silk winds along the path; a young woman in plain clothes walks behind an elaborately robed maid. A nearly full moon rises over reeds, and an empty basket rests on the ground by a willow.

name: Abundance
essence: You are at a high point of fullness; enjoy it without sorrow, and act clearly while the light is at its height.
judgment: Abundance brings success; the king attains it; be not sad, be like the sun at midday. Fullness never lasts, since noon gives way to evening, but grieving over that wastes the brightness you have, so shine on everything now.
image: Thunder and lightning arrive together, and the wise one decides disputes and carries out judgments. When clarity and energy coincide, it is the moment to settle matters decisively and fairly.

counsel.love: This is a rich season for love; celebrate it openly and generously, without worrying about whether it can last.
counsel.work: You are at the peak of your influence; make the important decisions now, while you have both clarity and momentum.
counsel.money: Plenty has come; enjoy it, but use the high tide to set aside for the ebb that inevitably follows.
counsel.health: Your vitality is strong; use it well, and remember that even the noon sun must set, so keep good rest in the rhythm.
counsel.family: Gather people and share your bounty; a full table now creates memories that will sustain the family through leaner times.
counsel.creativity: You are in a period of overflowing output; make and finish as much as you can while the light is bright.
counsel.study: Understanding is flooding in; consolidate it with notes and practice, so that the insight remains after the high point passes.
counsel.travel: A grand, festive journey is favoured; see the sights in full light and enjoy the abundance of the place.
counsel.spirit: Accept fullness without guilt or fear of its passing; noon is as sacred as dawn.
counsel.conflict: Settle the matter now with clarity and fairness; delay will only let the advantage fade.
counsel.decision: Lean yes, and act promptly while conditions are at their best; don't wait for a brighter hour that won't come.
counsel.timing: Now, at high noon in midsummer; the moment is full and will not stay that way.

lines: You meet your matching ruler. Even for ten days together there is no fault; joining with an equal partner brings recognition.
The curtain is so thick that the polestar is seen at noon. Your light is hidden by others; pushing forward brings suspicion, but sincere truth will win them over.
The undergrowth is so dense that small stars appear at noon; the right arm is broken. You cannot act through no fault of your own; wait it out.
The curtain is so thick that the polestar is seen at noon; you meet your ruler of like kind. The darkness lifts as you find the right ally; good fortune.
Brilliance draws near; blessing and fame come. By welcoming capable people, you gather lasting good fortune.
The house is full, the family screened off; peering through the gate, all is silent, and for three years nothing is seen. Abundance turned to isolation and pride leads to misfortune.
scene: Midsummer noon above a ripening river valley: the sun blazes overhead while a thunderstorm crackles at the edges of the sky, lightning flashing gold. A great timber hall stands open, its tables piled with fruit and grain, banners flying. People crowd its courtyard in bright clothing, and the heavy fields shimmer in heat.

name: The Wanderer
essence: You are a stranger passing through; be modest, careful and courteous, and you will find shelter wherever you go.
judgment: The wanderer has success through small things, and steadiness brings good fortune. With no home ground to stand on, you get by through good manners, discretion and lightness, not through claiming much.
image: Fire burns on the mountain, moving on and never staying long, and the wise one is clear-minded and careful in imposing penalties and does not drag out disputes. Treat everything as a passage: be decisive and fair, then move on without lingering in quarrels.

counsel.love: This may be a passing connection or a love lived at a distance; enjoy it honestly and lightly, without demanding permanence.
counsel.work: You are temporary or new; be pleasant, competent and discreet, and don't involve yourself in local politics.
counsel.money: Travel light financially; keep your assets portable and your commitments small until you know where you will settle.
counsel.health: Being on the move strains the body; protect your sleep, your water and your routines as you would a traveller's pack.
counsel.family: You may feel like an outsider at home or far from kin; small, steady gestures of contact will keep the thread unbroken.
counsel.creativity: New places and fresh eyes feed your work; keep a sketchbook, gather impressions, and don't force a grand plan yet.
counsel.study: Learn as a visitor does, attentive and humble; short courses and field study suit this time better than a settled programme.
counsel.travel: This is the travel hexagram; go, but keep your belongings secure, your manners good and your plans modest.
counsel.spirit: Every life is a sojourn; holding your possessions and opinions lightly makes you freer.
counsel.conflict: Settle quickly and fairly; as an outsider you gain nothing from prolonged disputes.
counsel.decision: Lean yes for small, temporary steps; lean no for anything that requires you to put down deep roots right now.
counsel.timing: Soon but briefly, like a grass fire on a hillside in late autumn: it moves quickly and doesn't stay.

lines: The wanderer busies himself with trivial things. Pettiness and fussing on the road draw misfortune; keep your dignity.
The wanderer comes to an inn with his goods and wins a loyal young servant. Modesty finds you shelter, means and help.
The inn burns down; the young servant is lost; danger. Arrogance and meddling as a guest cost you your place.
The wanderer finds a resting place, gains goods and an axe, yet his heart is not glad. You have security but not belonging; stay alert.
He shoots a pheasant; it falls with the first arrow; in the end praise and office. One graceful, well-judged act wins you a place among strangers.
The bird's nest burns. The wanderer laughs first and then wails; he loses his ox through carelessness. Heedless pride on the road brings misfortune.
scene: A late-autumn evening on a mountain road: a lone traveller with a staff and bundle walks past a wayside inn while, on the ridge above, a grass fire runs in a thin orange line against a dusky sky. A pheasant rises from bracken. Bare trees, a small lantern at the inn's door and long purple shadows.

name: The Gentle
essence: Gentle, steady influence that keeps blowing in one direction will reach further now than any sudden force.
judgment: The gentle brings success through small things; it furthers to have somewhere to go and to see the great person. Like wind that slips into every crack, your effect will come from consistent, quiet direction, and from aligning yourself with someone wise.
image: Winds follow one upon another, and the wise one spreads their instructions and carries out their undertakings. Repeated, clear and patient communication sinks in where a single loud command would not.

counsel.love: Win hearts gently and consistently; small attentions repeated over time will reach deeper than grand gestures.
counsel.work: Influence through persuasion, clear explanation and follow-up; know exactly what you want and keep returning to it calmly.
counsel.money: Small, regular contributions in one clear direction work best; don't keep switching strategies.
counsel.health: Gentle, consistent practices like breathing, stretching and walking every day penetrate deeper than strenuous bursts.
counsel.family: Soft persistence will shift a family pattern; make the same kind request clearly and patiently until it takes root.
counsel.creativity: Subtle refinement is your tool; revise in many light passes, letting the work become clearer each time.
counsel.study: Repetition is the method: short sessions every day, reviewing until the knowledge permeates.
counsel.travel: Go where you have a clear purpose, ideally to meet someone you can learn from; keep the itinerary flexible as the wind.
counsel.spirit: Yield to the deeper current rather than resisting; humility opens you to guidance.
counsel.conflict: Find what is hidden and bring it gently into light; avoid both endless dithering and blunt force.
counsel.decision: Lean yes, if you can commit to a clear direction and see it through; indecision is the danger here.
counsel.timing: Gradually, like a steady spring breeze that ripens the fields day after day; three days before and three days after the turning.

lines: Advancing and retreating. Indecision weakens you; adopt a soldier's resolve and choose your direction.
Penetration under the bed; priests and diviners in great numbers. Trace hidden influences to their source and name them; good fortune, no blame.
Repeated penetration. Endless pondering and second-guessing bring humiliation; decide.
Regret vanishes; in the hunt, three kinds of game are caught. Modest, energetic effort yields results for everyone.
Steadiness brings good fortune; no beginning but an end. Weigh carefully three days before a change and review three days after; good fortune.
Penetration under the bed; he loses his goods and his axe. Digging too far into hidden things drains your strength; persisting brings misfortune.
scene: A spring hillside where gusts of wind move through tall grass and a stand of bamboo in long silver waves, one following another. Pale green willow branches stream sideways, kites hang in a soft blue sky, and a robed messenger walks the path with banners fluttering. Petals and seeds drift through the light.

name: The Joyous
essence: Genuine gladness, shared openly and grounded in sincerity, is your strength now.
judgment: The joyous brings success, and steadiness furthers. Joy that rests on inner firmness and outward gentleness wins people over willingly, without force, but joy that is only flattery or excess soon goes sour.
image: Two lakes rest against each other, refreshing one another, and the wise one joins with friends for discussion and practice. Learning and delight grow best in good company, where each person keeps the other lively and honest.

counsel.love: Laugh together and speak your affection plainly; joy that is sincere draws you closer, while teasing that wounds does not.
counsel.work: Lead with encouragement; a cheerful, open team will accomplish more than a pressured one.
counsel.money: Spend on shared experiences rather than display, and beware of offers that are pleasing on the surface but empty underneath.
counsel.health: Joy and companionship are good medicine; meet friends, sing, walk by water, and keep pleasures within healthy limits.
counsel.family: Gather people for conversation and play; let gladness be the glue, not obligation.
counsel.creativity: Make work that delights you; collaboration and exchange with peers will spark your best ideas.
counsel.study: Study with friends; discussing and practising together makes learning both deeper and more enjoyable.
counsel.travel: A trip with good company to a place near water is favoured; savour it, but don't overindulge.
counsel.spirit: True joy is inward and steady, not dependent on excitement; cultivate the quiet gladness that remains when the party ends.
counsel.conflict: Friendly words will open what argument cannot, but don't be lured by charm into a bad bargain.
counsel.decision: Lean yes if the choice brings genuine, lasting joy; lean no if it only flatters you or offers a passing thrill.
counsel.timing: Soon and pleasantly, like a clear autumn afternoon by the lake when the harvest is in.

lines: Contented joyousness. Quiet, self-sufficient gladness that asks for nothing; good fortune.
Sincere joyousness. Joy rooted in truth keeps you from shabby pleasures; regret vanishes.
Joyousness that comes seeking. Chasing pleasures from outside empties you; misfortune.
Joyousness that is weighed is not at peace. Choose firmly between higher and lower pleasures; once you reject the harmful, real joy follows.
Trusting what disintegrates brings danger. Be wary of charming influences that wear away at what is good.
Seductive joyousness. You are being led along by pleasure; notice where it is taking you.
scene: Two calm lakes side by side in a golden autumn afternoon, joined by a narrow channel and reflecting a soft sky. On a wooden pavilion between them, friends sit with tea and scrolls, laughing and talking; one plays a flute. Ducks drift on bright water, reeds glow, and a gentle breeze ruffles their robes.

name: Dispersion
essence: Rigid walls between people, or within you, are ready to melt; let what is frozen thaw and gather around something higher.
judgment: Dispersion brings success: the king approaches his temple, and it furthers to cross the great water. Selfishness and division are dissolved when people turn together toward a shared purpose or a sacred centre, and the result is movement, even across great obstacles.
image: Wind blows over the water, scattering foam and loosening ice, and the kings of old offered sacrifice and built temples. Shared ritual and devotion break up hard hearts and draw scattered people back into one body.

counsel.love: Let go of stubbornness and old grudges; a shared ritual, trip or celebration can melt the distance between you.
counsel.work: Break down silos and egos; gather the team around a common mission rather than individual agendas.
counsel.money: Loosen your grip a little; spread resources wisely, give generously, and release what you cling to out of fear.
counsel.health: Release tension: warmth, sweat, movement and breath help dissolve what is stuck in body and mood.
counsel.family: Scattered relatives can be drawn together by an occasion: a meal, a memorial, a festival that everyone shares.
counsel.creativity: Dissolve the rigid plan; let the work flow and spread out before you shape it again.
counsel.study: Break up a block by changing setting or joining a group; fresh air dissolves mental fog.
counsel.travel: A crossing over water or a pilgrimage is especially favoured; journeys that reunite people are blessed.
counsel.spirit: This is a time to dissolve the ego's hard shell in devotion; worship, music and service bring you home.
counsel.conflict: Seek reconciliation through a shared higher aim; let factional pride melt rather than digging in.
counsel.decision: Lean yes for anything that unites or releases; lean no for anything that hardens divisions.
counsel.timing: Soon, like spring wind loosening the river ice; once the thaw begins, things move quickly.

lines: He brings help with the strength of a horse. Act early and vigorously to stop division before it spreads; good fortune.
At the time of dispersion he hurries to his support. Run to what steadies you, people or principles; regret vanishes.
He dissolves his self. Setting aside your own interest for a larger task leaves no regret.
He dissolves his bond with his faction; supreme good fortune. Dispersion gathers into a hill, which ordinary people cannot imagine; letting go of a group builds a larger whole.
His loud cries dissolve like sweat; the king's dwelling is dispersed. A great, freeing word from the centre breaks the deadlock; no blame.
He dissolves his blood, going far away and out. Remove yourself and those close to you from danger; no blame.
scene: A wide river in early spring where wind pushes over the water, breaking sheets of ice into drifting floes and spray. A ferry boat full of people crosses toward a temple on the far bank, its incense smoke streaming sideways. On the near shore a horse gallops along the bank. Pale sun breaks through scattering clouds.

name: Limitation
essence: Good limits give your life shape and strength; set them wisely, not harshly, and keep to them gladly.
judgment: Limitation brings success, but limits that are bitter must not be persisted in. Like the joints of bamboo that make it strong, measure gives structure, but rules so severe that they choke life will not last.
image: Water rests above the lake, which holds only so much before it overflows, and the wise one creates number and measure and examines the nature of virtue and right conduct. Know your capacity and set clear standards that fit it.

counsel.love: Healthy boundaries make love safer and freer; agree on what you each need, without turning it into a list of rules.
counsel.work: Define your scope, hours and priorities; doing fewer things with full care serves you better than unlimited commitment.
counsel.money: Make a budget you can actually live with; a sensible measure honoured every month beats a strict one abandoned in a week.
counsel.health: Moderation is the medicine: enough sleep, measured portions, and limits on what drains you, applied kindly.
counsel.family: Clear, fair household rules reduce friction; review any that have become harsh or outdated.
counsel.creativity: Constraints sharpen your art; set a form, a word count or a palette, and let the limits do their work.
counsel.study: Set a realistic schedule with defined sessions and breaks, and keep it consistently.
counsel.travel: Plan within your means and time; a well-paced, bounded trip will be more enjoyable than an overstuffed one.
counsel.spirit: Self-discipline that feels sweet rather than punishing is a sign you are on the right path.
counsel.conflict: Know where the line is, and hold it calmly; neither give away too much nor demand what is excessive.
counsel.decision: Lean yes, within clear limits; decide how far you will go before you start.
counsel.timing: In measured steps, like the knots of bamboo growing one segment at a time; things come at the pace you set.

lines: Not going out of the door and courtyard. Knowing when to stay inside the limits and keep silent: no blame.
Not going out of the gate and courtyard. Holding back when the moment calls for action: misfortune.
He who knows no limits will have cause to lament. Indulgence brings sorrow you made yourself; if you accept the blame, there is no further fault.
Contented limitation. Accepting measure naturally, without strain; success.
Sweet limitation. Limits you apply first to yourself, gently, bring good fortune and win others' respect.
Bitter limitation. Severity carried too far brings misfortune if persisted in, though in rare cases it spares you remorse.
scene: A terraced garden beside a still lake at the start of winter, with a bamboo grove whose segmented stalks are drawn in crisp detail. Stone channels and a small sluice gate regulate water from the hills into the lake, which brims exactly to its edge. A courtyard door stands half open, a lantern beside it, morning frost on the steps.

name: Inner Truth
essence: An open, sincere heart can reach even the hardest-to-reach people; let your truth be quiet and unforced.
judgment: Inner truth: pigs and fishes, good fortune; it furthers to cross the great water, and steadiness furthers. Even creatures that seem dull and unreachable can be moved when the heart is truly empty of guile, and that sincerity is strong enough to carry you across great difficulties.
image: Wind moves over the lake, stirring its whole surface, and the wise one deliberates over legal cases in order to delay executions. Understanding someone from within brings mercy, and real influence comes from entering into another person's situation.

counsel.love: Speak and listen from the heart; your unguarded sincerity is the bridge to someone who seems hard to reach.
counsel.work: Earn trust through honesty and by truly understanding others' needs; this will carry a difficult project across.
counsel.money: Deal only where there is mutual trust; transparency on both sides protects you better than clever terms.
counsel.health: Listen honestly to your body and emotions; an open, unhurried inner check-in reveals what you need.
counsel.family: Like a crane calling to its young, a sincere word spoken at home is answered; reach out first.
counsel.creativity: Make work that comes from a true, inward place; audiences sense sincerity and respond to it.
counsel.study: Enter into the mind of the author or teacher; empathy with the material leads to real understanding.
counsel.travel: A long journey or a crossing is favoured, especially one taken to reconcile or to meet someone in person.
counsel.spirit: Empty yourself of pretence; the hollow centre of this hexagram is the space where truth can enter.
counsel.conflict: Seek to understand your opponent's position from the inside; mercy and comprehension will resolve more than punishment.
counsel.decision: Lean yes if you can act with full honesty and good faith; if something hidden is involved, wait.
counsel.timing: Soon, when trust has formed; like a crane's call over a lake at dusk, the answer comes when your call is true.

lines: Being prepared brings good fortune; hidden designs bring unrest. Rely on your own inner centre rather than secret alliances.
A crane calls in the shade; its young one answers. I have a fine cup; I will share it with you. True feeling finds its echo across distance.
He finds a companion; now he beats the drum, now he stops, now he weeps, now he sings. Depending on others for your inner balance makes your moods swing.
The moon is nearly full; the team horse goes astray. Turn toward a higher purpose even if it means leaving a partner; no blame.
He possesses truth that links others together. A sincerity that binds people firmly; no blame.
The cock's crow rises toward heaven. Words that claim more than the heart contains; persisting brings misfortune.
scene: Dusk over a calm lake in early autumn, a gentle wind stirring silver ripples. On a reed bank in shadow, a crane calls with lifted head while its young answers from the water. Carp break the surface; a few pigs root near a farmhouse on the shore. A nearly full moon rises, and a boat waits at the jetty.

name: Preponderance of the Small
essence: This is a time for small, careful steps and extra humility; do not fly high, stay close to the ground.
judgment: Small exceeding brings success, and steadiness furthers: small things may be done, but not great ones. The flying bird leaves this message: it is not good to strive upward, it is good to stay below, and then there is great good fortune.
image: Thunder rumbles on the mountain, muffled and near, and the wise one leans a little toward excess in reverence, in grief and in thrift. When the time is narrow, err on the side of modesty, care and restraint.

counsel.love: Show love in small, attentive ways rather than grand declarations; humility and courtesy will be warmly received.
counsel.work: Do the details exceptionally well and avoid ambitious leaps; this is not the time for bold expansion.
counsel.money: Be thrifty and conservative; a little more caution than seems necessary will serve you well.
counsel.health: Be gentle with your body; small adjustments and careful habits are wiser now than dramatic regimes.
counsel.family: Show a little extra respect to elders and a little extra patience at home; small courtesies matter greatly now.
counsel.creativity: Work in miniature or refine details; precise, modest pieces will succeed where a grand project would falter.
counsel.study: Concentrate on details and basics; careful, humble review is better than leaping ahead.
counsel.travel: Keep journeys short and close to home; stay low, literally and figuratively, and be extra careful.
counsel.spirit: Humility and reverence are the practice; bow a little lower than you think you must.
counsel.conflict: Avoid escalation; defend carefully, watch your back, and do not reach for a decisive blow.
counsel.decision: Lean yes only for small, modest steps; lean no for anything ambitious or high-risk.
counsel.timing: Not yet for big things; like low thunder in the hills before rain, the moment for small actions is now and for great ones later.

lines: The bird meets misfortune by flying. Rising too early and too high brings trouble; stay in the nest.
He passes his ancestor and meets his ancestress; he does not reach the prince but meets the official. Keep to your proper level and accept indirect access; no blame.
If you are not extremely careful, someone may strike you from behind. Overconfidence invites harm; guard yourself; misfortune otherwise.
No blame; he meets him without passing by. Going forward is dangerous; be on guard, do not act, keep steady.
Dense clouds but no rain from the western lands; the prince shoots and takes the one in the cave. You cannot accomplish it alone; seek capable helpers who have been hidden.
He passes by without meeting; the flying bird leaves him. Overreaching beyond all measure brings calamity and injury.
scene: A late-spring afternoon in rocky hills under low, heavy clouds that do not rain. Muffled thunder rolls over a small mountain. A sparrow flutters low over the grass rather than soaring; a hunter crouches at the mouth of a cave with a short bow. In the foreground, a careful figure bows at a modest roadside shrine.

name: After Completion
essence: You have crossed and things are in order; now the work is to stay alert, because what is finished begins at once to unravel.
judgment: After completion there is success in small matters, and steadiness furthers: good fortune at the beginning, disorder at the end. Every line is in its proper place, a perfect balance, which is exactly why careless relaxing will tip it over.
image: Water stands over fire, the kettle boiling as it should, and the wise one thinks of misfortune and guards against it in advance. Keep the fire and the water in balance; tend them, or they will boil over or go out.

counsel.love: The relationship has reached a good place; keep tending it in small ways rather than assuming it will maintain itself.
counsel.work: The project is done or the goal reached; document it, maintain it and watch for small problems before they grow.
counsel.money: Your finances are in order; protect them with routine checks and avoid relaxing into complacency or risky new bets.
counsel.health: You have recovered or reached your goal; maintenance habits now keep you from sliding back.
counsel.family: Home is settled; keep up the small attentions and routines that hold it together.
counsel.creativity: The work is finished; polish small details, resist overworking it, and protect it from careless changes.
counsel.study: You have learned the material; review regularly so that it is not lost.
counsel.travel: You have arrived; settle in carefully, keep your belongings secure, and don't let a good trip end in carelessness.
counsel.spirit: Do not mistake a moment of clarity for final arrival; keep practising, as the mind slips back easily.
counsel.conflict: The dispute is settled; don't reopen it, and stay watchful for minor sparks that could restart it.
counsel.decision: Lean toward keeping things as they are; small adjustments only, not new big ventures.
counsel.timing: It has already happened; like the hour after harvest, the task now is to store well and watch for frost.

lines: He brakes his wheels; the fox gets its tail wet. Don't rush ahead in the first flush of success; no blame.
The woman loses her carriage curtain. Do not run after it; on the seventh day it returns. Wait without forcing recognition.
The Illustrious Ancestor disciplines the Devil's Country; after three years he conquers. Great efforts drag on; do not employ small-minded people.
Fine garments turn to rags. Be careful all day long; small leaks show that decline has begun.
The eastern neighbour slaughters an ox; it does not equal the western neighbour's simple offering. Sincerity counts for more than display.
He gets his head in the water; danger. Looking back proudly once the crossing is done invites disaster; keep moving forward.
scene: A quiet harvest evening in a farmhouse kitchen: an iron kettle steams on a carefully banked fire, everything neatly in its place, jars sealed and shelves stocked. Through the open door a river shines, a carriage stands on the far bank having just crossed, and a fox shakes its wet tail on the bank. A single lamp glows.

name: Before Completion
essence: You are almost across but not yet; go carefully, sort things into their proper places, and the crossing will be made.
judgment: Before completion there is success, but if the little fox, nearly across, gets its tail wet, nothing furthers. The promise is real and the end is in sight, so the danger now is the careless last step, and caution with clear discernment will carry you over.
image: Fire is above the water, each heading its own way, and the wise one carefully distinguishes things so that each finds its place. Order has not yet been made; your task is to understand the nature of each part and set it where it belongs.

counsel.love: The relationship is still forming; be patient and attentive, and don't force a conclusion before both of you are ready.
counsel.work: The project is close but not finished; check every detail, put the right people in the right roles, and don't celebrate early.
counsel.money: You are in a transition; avoid rash final moves and sort out your accounts carefully before committing.
counsel.health: Recovery or change is under way but incomplete; keep up the care and don't stop the moment you feel better.
counsel.family: Things are shifting at home; help each person find their place and be patient with what remains unsettled.
counsel.creativity: The piece is almost there; take time over the final passes, and keep the freshness of something still becoming.
counsel.study: You are near the end of a course; review thoroughly rather than coasting through the last stretch.
counsel.travel: Mind the last leg of the journey; the final crossing is where mistakes happen, so travel with care.
counsel.spirit: Every ending is also a beginning; the open, unfinished state is full of promise if held with care.
counsel.conflict: Resolution is near but not reached; avoid a premature attack, and sort out exactly what each side needs.
counsel.decision: Lean wait a little, then yes; prepare carefully first, and the move will succeed when everything is in place.
counsel.timing: Not yet, but soon; like the last weeks of winter when the ice is thin and spring is close, step carefully.

lines: He gets his tail wet. Starting before you are ready leads to humiliation; hold back.
He brakes his wheels. Patient restraint while the time matures; steadiness brings good fortune.
Before completion, attacking brings misfortune, yet it furthers to cross the great water. You cannot force it alone; change your approach and seek new support.
Steadiness brings good fortune and regret vanishes. Like thunder disciplining the Devil's Country, three years of firm struggle are rewarded with great realms.
Steadiness brings good fortune and no regret. The light of the noble one is true; your sincerity wins, good fortune.
Drinking wine in genuine confidence; no blame. But if he wets his head, he loses it. Celebrate the coming success, without losing yourself in excess.
scene: Late winter at twilight: a young red fox picks its way across a frozen river on thinning ice, its tail held high just above dark open water. On the far bank, a campfire burns beside bare trees, flames reflected in the water below. The first pale stars appear, and loose ice floes drift between the two shores.
